abdominal aorta.meaning: portion of the aorta inferior to the aortic hiatus and superior to the common iliac arteries

abdominopelvic cavity.meaning: division of the anterior (ventral) cavity that houses the abdominal and pelvic viscera

abducens nerve.meaning: sixth cranial nerve; responsible for contraction of one of the extraocular muscles

abduct.meaning: move away from midline in the sagittal plane

abduction.meaning: movement in the coronal plane that moves a limb laterally away from the body; spreading of the fingers

abductor.meaning: moves the bone away from the midline

abductor digiti minimi.meaning: muscle that abducts the little finger

abductor pollicis longus.meaning: muscle that inserts into the first metacarpal

abo blood group.meaning: blood-type classification based on the presence or absence of A and B glycoproteins on the erythrocyte membrane surface

absolute refractory period.meaning: time during an action period when another action potential cannot be generated because the voltage-gated Na+ channel is inactivated

absorption.meaning: passage of digested products from the intestinal lumen through mucosal cells and into the bloodstream or lacteals

absorptive state.meaning: also called the fed state; the metabolic state occurring during the first few hours after ingesting food in which the body is digesting food and absorbing the nutrients

accessory digestive organ.meaning: includes teeth, tongue, salivary glands, gallbladder, liver, and pancreas

accessory duct.meaning: (also, duct of Santorini) duct that runs from the pancreas into the duodenum

acclimatisation.meaning: process of adjustment that the respiratory system makes due to chronic exposure to high altitudes

accommodation.meaning: in vision, a change in the ability of the eye to focus on objects at different distances

accommodation–convergence reflex.meaning: coordination of somatic control of the medial rectus muscles of either eye with the parasympathetic control of the ciliary bodies to maintain focus while the eyes converge on visual stimuli near to the face

acetabular labrum.meaning: lip of fibrocartilage that surrounds outer margin of the acetabulum on the hip bone

acetabulum.meaning: large, cup-shaped cavity located on the lateral side of the hip bone; formed by the junction of the ilium, pubis, and ischium portions of the hip bone

acetyl coenzyme a (acetyl coa).meaning: starting molecule of the Krebs cycle

acetylcholine.meaning: neurotransmitter that binds at a motor end-plate to trigger depolarisation

acid.meaning: compound that releases hydrogen ions (H+) in solution

acinus.meaning: cluster of glandular epithelial cells in the pancreas that secretes pancreatic juice in the pancreas

acne.meaning: skin condition due to infected sebaceous glands

acromegaly.meaning: disorder in adults caused when abnormally high levels of GH trigger growth of bones in the face, hands, and feet

acromial end of the clavicle.meaning: lateral end of the clavicle that articulates with the acromion of the scapula

acromioclavicular joint.meaning: articulation between the acromion of the scapula and the acromial end of the clavicle

acromion.meaning: flattened bony process that extends laterally from the scapular spine to form the bony tip of the shoulder

acrosomal reaction.meaning: release of digestive enzymes by sperm that enables them to burrow through the corona radiata and penetrate the zona pellucida of an oocyte prior to fertilisation

acrosome.meaning: cap-like vesicle located at the anterior-most region of a sperm that is rich with lysosomal enzymes capable of digesting the protective layers surrounding the oocyte

actin.meaning: protein that makes up most of the thin myofilaments in a sarcomere muscle fibre

action potential.meaning: change in voltage of a cell membrane in response to a stimulus that results in transmission of an electrical signal; unique to neurons and muscle fibres

activation energy.meaning: amount of energy greater than the energy contained in the reactants, which must be overcome for a reaction to proceed

activation gate.meaning: part of the voltage-gated Na+ channel that opens when the membrane voltage reaches threshold

active immunity.meaning: immunity developed from an individual’s own immune system

active transport.meaning: form of transport across the cell membrane that requires input of cellular energy

acute inflammation.meaning: inflammation occurring for a limited time period; rapidly developing

acute mountain sickness.meaning: condition that occurs a result of acute exposure to high altitude due to a low partial pressure of oxygen

adaptive immune response.meaning: relatively slow but very specific and effective immune response controlled by lymphocytes

adduction.meaning: movement in the coronal plane that moves a limb medially toward or across the midline of the body; bringing fingers together

adductor.meaning: moves the bone toward the midline

adductor brevis.meaning: muscle that adducts and medially rotates the thigh

adductor longus.meaning: muscle that adducts, medially rotates, and flexes the thigh

adductor magnus.meaning: muscle with an anterior fascicle that adducts, medially rotates and flexes the thigh, and a posterior fascicle that assists in thigh extension

adductor tubercle.meaning: small, bony bump located on the superior aspect of the medial epicondyle of the femur

adenosine triphosphate.meaning: nucleotide containing ribose and an adenine base that is essential in energy transfer

adenylyl cyclase.meaning: membrane-bound enzyme that converts ATP to cyclic AMP, creating cAMP, as a result of G-protein activation

adipose tissue.meaning: specialised areolar tissue rich in stored fat

adrenal artery.meaning: branch of the abdominal aorta; supplies blood to the adrenal (suprarenal) glands

adrenal cortex.meaning: outer region of the adrenal glands consisting of multiple layers of epithelial cells and capillary networks that produces mineralocorticoids and glucocorticoids

adrenal glands.meaning: endocrine glands located at the top of each kidney that are important for the regulation of the stress response, blood pressure and blood volume, water homeostasis, and electrolyte levels

adrenal medulla.meaning: interior portion of the adrenal (or suprarenal) gland that releases epinephrine and norepinephrine into the bloodstream as hormones

adrenal vein.meaning: drains the adrenal or suprarenal glands that are immediately superior to the kidneys; the right adrenal vein enters the inferior vena cava directly and the left adrenal vein enters the left renal vein

adrenergic.meaning: synapse where norepinephrine is released, which binds to α- or β-adrenergic receptors

adrenocorticotropic hormone.meaning: anterior pituitary hormone that stimulates the adrenal cortex to secrete corticosteroid hormones (also called corticotropin)

aerobic respiration.meaning: production of ATP in the presence of oxygen

afferent branch.meaning: component of a reflex arc that represents the input from a sensory neuron, for either a special or general sense

afterbirth.meaning: third stage of childbirth in which the placenta and associated fetal membranes are expelled

afterload.meaning: force the ventricles must develop to effectively pump blood against the resistance in the vessels

agglutination.meaning: clustering of cells into masses linked by antibodies

agonist.meaning: (also, prime mover) muscle whose contraction is responsible for producing a particular motion

agranular leukocytes.meaning: leukocytes with few granules in their cytoplasm; specifically, monocytes, lymphocytes, and NK cells

ala.meaning: (plural = alae) small, flaring structure of a nostril that forms the lateral side of the nares

alar cartilage.meaning: cartilage that supports the apex of the nose and helps shape the nares; it is connected to the septal cartilage and connective tissue of the alae

alar plate.meaning: developmental region of the spinal cord that gives rise to the posterior horn of the grey matter

alarm reaction.meaning: the short-term stress, or the fight-or-flight response, of stage one of the general adaptation syndrome mediated by the hormones epinephrine and norepinephrine

albinism.meaning: genetic disorder that affects the skin, in which there is no melanin production

albumin.meaning: most abundant plasma protein, accounting for most of the osmotic pressure of plasma

aldosterone.meaning: hormone produced and secreted by the adrenal cortex that stimulates sodium and fluid retention and increases blood volume and blood pressure

alimentary canal.meaning: continuous muscular digestive tube that extends from the mouth to the anus

alkaloid.meaning: substance, usually from a plant source, that is chemically basic with respect to pH and will stimulate bitter receptors

allantois.meaning: finger-like outpocketing of yolk sac forms the primitive excretory duct of the embryo; precursor to the urinary bladder

allele.meaning: alternative forms of a gene that occupy a specific locus on a specific gene

alpha (α)-adrenergic receptor.meaning: one of the receptors to which epinephrine and norepinephrine bind, which comes in two subtypes: α1 and α2

alpha cell.meaning: pancreatic islet cell type that produces the hormone glucagon

alveolar dead space.meaning: air space within alveoli that are unable to participate in gas exchange

alveolar duct.meaning: small tube that leads from the terminal bronchiole to the respiratory bronchiole and is the point of attachment for alveoli

alveolar macrophage.meaning: immune system cell of the alveolus that removes debris and pathogens

alveolar pore.meaning: opening that allows airflow between neighbouring alveoli

alveolar process of the mandible.meaning: upper border of mandibular body that contains the lower teeth

alveolar process of the maxilla.meaning: curved, inferior margin of the maxilla that supports and anchors the upper teeth

alveoli.meaning: (of the breast) milk-secreting cells in the mammary gland

alveolus.meaning: small, grape-like sac that performs gas exchange in the lungs

amacrine cell.meaning: type of cell in the retina that connects to the bipolar cells near the outer synaptic layer and provides the basis for early image processing within the retina

amino acid.meaning: building block of proteins; characterised by an amino and carboxyl functional groups and a variable side-chain

aminopeptidase.meaning: brush border enzyme that acts on proteins

amnion.meaning: transparent membranous sac that encloses the developing fetus and fills with amniotic fluid

amniotic cavity.meaning: cavity that opens up between the inner cell mass and the trophoblast; develops into amnion

amphipathic.meaning: describes a molecule that exhibits a difference in polarity between its two ends, resulting in a difference in water solubility

ampulla.meaning: (of the uterine tube) middle portion of the uterine tube in which fertilisation often occurs

amygdala.meaning: nucleus deep in the temporal lobe of the cerebrum that is related to memory and emotional behaviour

anabolic hormones.meaning: hormones that stimulate the synthesis of new, larger molecules

anabolic reactions.meaning: reactions that build smaller molecules into larger molecules

anabolism.meaning: assembly of more complex molecules from simpler molecules

anaemia.meaning: deficiency of red blood cells or haemoglobin

anagen.meaning: active phase of the hair growth cycle

anal canal.meaning: final segment of the large intestine

anal column.meaning: long fold of mucosa in the anal canal

anal triangle.meaning: posterior triangle of the perineum that includes the anus

anaphase.meaning: third stage of mitosis (and meiosis), during which sister chromatids separate into two new nuclear regions of a dividing cell

anaphylactic shock.meaning: type of shock that follows a severe allergic reaction and results from massive vasodilation

anastomosis.meaning: (plural = anastomoses) area where vessels unite to allow blood to circulate even if there may be partial blockage in another branch

anatomical dead space.meaning: air space present in the airway that never reaches the alveoli and therefore never participates in gas exchange

anatomical neck.meaning: line on the humerus located around the outside margin of the humeral head

anatomical position.meaning: standard reference position used for describing locations and directions on the human body

anatomical sphincter.meaning: smooth or skeletal muscle surrounding the lumen of a vessel or hollow organ that can restrict flow when contracted

anatomy.meaning: science that studies the form and composition of the body’s structures

anchoring junction.meaning: mechanically attaches adjacent cells to each other or to the basement membrane

anconeus.meaning: small muscle on the lateral posterior elbow that extends the forearm

angioblasts.meaning: stem cells that give rise to blood vessels

angiotensin i.meaning: protein produced by the enzymatic action of renin on angiotensinogen; inactive precursor of angiotensin II

angiotensin ii.meaning: protein produced by the enzymatic action of ACE on inactive angiotensin I; actively causes vasoconstriction and stimulates aldosterone release by the adrenal cortex

angiotensin-converting enzyme.meaning: enzyme produced by the lungs that catalyses the reaction of inactive angiotensin I into active angiotensin II

angiotensinogen.meaning: inactive protein in the circulation produced by the liver; precursor of angiotensin I; must be modified by the enzymes renin and ACE to be activated

angle of the mandible.meaning: rounded corner located at outside margin of the body and ramus junction

angle of the rib.meaning: portion of rib with greatest curvature; together, the rib angles form the most posterior extent of the thoracic cage

ankle joint.meaning: joint that separates the leg and foot portions of the lower limb; formed by the articulations between the talus bone of the foot inferiorly, and the distal end of the tibia, medial malleolus of the tibia, and lateral malleolus of the fibula superiorly

annular ligament.meaning: intrinsic ligament of the elbow articular capsule that surrounds and supports the head of the radius at the proximal radioulnar joint

anosmia.meaning: loss of the sense of smell; usually the result of physical disruption of the first cranial nerve

antagonist.meaning: muscle that opposes the action of an agonist

anterior.meaning: describes the front or direction toward the front of the body; also referred to as ventral

anterior (ventral) sacral foramen.meaning: one of the series of paired openings located on the anterior (ventral) side of the sacrum

anterior arch.meaning: anterior portion of the ring-like C1 (atlas) vertebra

anterior border of the tibia.meaning: narrow, anterior margin of the tibia that extends inferiorly from the tibial tuberosity

anterior cardiac veins.meaning: vessels that parallel the small cardiac arteries and drain the anterior surface of the right ventricle; bypass the coronary sinus and drain directly into the right atrium

anterior cavity.meaning: larger body cavity located anterior to the posterior (dorsal) body cavity; includes the serous membrane-lined pleural cavities for the lungs, pericardial cavity for the heart, and peritoneal cavity for the abdominal and pelvic organs; also referred to as ventral cavity

anterior cerebral artery.meaning: arises from the internal carotid artery; supplies the frontal lobe of the cerebrum

anterior column.meaning: white matter between the anterior horns of the spinal cord composed of many different groups of axons of both ascending and descending tracts

anterior communicating artery.meaning: anastomosis of the right and left internal carotid arteries; supplies blood to the brain

anterior compartment of the arm.meaning: (anterior flexor compartment of the arm) the biceps brachii, brachialis, brachioradialis, and their associated blood vessels and nerves

anterior compartment of the forearm.meaning: (anterior flexor compartment of the forearm) deep and superficial muscles that originate on the humerus and insert into the hand

anterior compartment of the leg.meaning: region that includes muscles that dorsiflex the foot

anterior compartment of the thigh.meaning: region that includes muscles that flex the thigh and extend the leg

anterior corticospinal tract.meaning: division of the corticospinal pathway that travels through the ventral (anterior) column of the spinal cord and controls axial musculature through the medial motor neurons in the ventral (anterior) horn

anterior cranial fossa.meaning: shallowest and most anterior cranial fossa of the cranial base that extends from the frontal bone to the lesser wing of the sphenoid bone

anterior cruciate ligament.meaning: intracapsular ligament of the knee; extends from anterior, superior surface of the tibia to the inner aspect of the lateral condyle of the femur; resists hyperextension of knee

anterior horn.meaning: grey matter of the spinal cord containing multipolar motor neurons, sometimes referred to as the ventral horn

anterior inferior iliac spine.meaning: small, bony projection located on the anterior margin of the ilium, below the anterior superior iliac spine

anterior interventricular artery.meaning: (also, left anterior descending artery or LAD) major branch of the left coronary artery that follows the anterior interventricular sulcus

anterior interventricular sulcus.meaning: sulcus located between the left and right ventricles on the anterior surface of the heart

anterior longitudinal ligament.meaning: ligament that runs the length of the vertebral column, uniting the anterior aspects of the vertebral bodies

anterior median fissure.meaning: deep midline feature of the anterior spinal cord, marking the separation between the right and left sides of the cord

anterior sacroiliac ligament.meaning: strong ligament between the sacrum and the ilium portions of the hip bone that supports the anterior side of the sacroiliac joint

anterior scalene.meaning: a muscle anterior to the middle scalene

anterior spinal artery.meaning: blood vessel from the merged branches of the vertebral arteries that runs along the anterior surface of the spinal cord

anterior superior iliac spine.meaning: rounded, anterior end of the iliac crest

anterior talofibular ligament.meaning: intrinsic ligament located on the lateral side of the ankle joint, between talus bone and lateral malleolus of fibula; supports talus at the talocrural joint and resists excess inversion of the foot

anterior tibial artery.meaning: branches from the popliteal artery; supplies blood to the anterior tibial region; becomes the dorsalis pedis artery

anterior tibial vein.meaning: forms from the dorsal venous arch; drains the area near the tibialis anterior muscle and leads to the popliteal vein

anterograde amnesia.meaning: inability to form new memories from a particular time forward

antibodies.meaning: (also, immunoglobulins or gamma globulins) antigen-specific proteins produced by specialised B lymphocytes that protect the body by binding to foreign objects such as bacteria and viruses

antibody.meaning: antigen-specific protein secreted by plasma cells; immunoglobulin

anticholinergic drugs.meaning: drugs that interrupt or reduce the function of the parasympathetic system

anticoagulant.meaning: substance such as heparin that opposes coagulation

anticodon.meaning: consecutive sequence of three nucleotides on a tRNA molecule that is complementary to a specific codon on an mRNA molecule

antidiuretic hormone.meaning: also known as vasopressin, a hormone that increases the volume of water reabsorbed from the collecting tubules of the kidney

antigen.meaning: molecule recognised by the receptors of B and T lymphocytes

antigen presentation.meaning: binding of processed antigen to the protein-binding cleft of a major histocompatibility complex molecule

antigen processing.meaning: internalisation and digestion of antigen in an antigen-presenting cell

antigen receptor.meaning: two-chain receptor by which lymphocytes recognise antigen

antigenic determinant.meaning: (also, epitope) one of the chemical groups recognised by a single type of lymphocyte antigen receptor

antithrombin.meaning: anticoagulant that inactivates factor X and opposes the conversion of prothrombin (factor II) into thrombin in the common pathway

antrum.meaning: fluid-filled chamber that characterises a mature tertiary (antral) follicle

anulus fibrosus.meaning: tough, fibrous outer portion of an intervertebral disc, which is strongly anchored to the bodies of the adjacent vertebrae

anuria.meaning: absence of urine produced; production of 50 mL or less per day

aorta.meaning: largest artery in the body, originating from the left ventricle and descending to the abdominal region where it bifurcates into the common iliac arteries at the level of the fourth lumbar vertebra; arteries originating from the aorta distribute blood to virtually all tissues of the body

aortic arch.meaning: arc that connects the ascending aorta to the descending aorta; ends at the intervertebral disc between the fourth and fifth thoracic vertebrae

aortic hiatus.meaning: opening in the diaphragm that allows passage of the thoracic aorta into the abdominal region where it becomes the abdominal aorta

aortic sinuses.meaning: small pockets in the ascending aorta near the aortic valve that are the locations of the baroreceptors (stretch receptors) and chemoreceptors that trigger a reflex that aids in the regulation of vascular homeostasis

aortic valve.meaning: (also, aortic semilunar valve) valve located at the base of the aorta

apical.meaning: that part of a cell or tissue which, in general, faces an open space

apical ectodermal ridge.meaning: enlarged ridge of ectoderm at the distal end of a limb bud that stimulates growth and elongation of the limb

apneustic centre.meaning: network of neurons within the pons that stimulate the neurons in the dorsal respiratory group; controls the depth of inspiration

apocrine secretion.meaning: release of a substance along with the apical portion of the cell

apocrine sweat gland.meaning: type of sweat gland that is associated with hair follicles in the armpits and genital regions

aponeurosis.meaning: broad, tendon-like sheet of connective tissue that attaches a skeletal muscle to another skeletal muscle or to a bone

appendicular skeleton.meaning: all bones of the upper and lower limbs, plus the girdle bones that attach each limb to the axial skeleton

appendix.meaning: (vermiform appendix) coiled tube attached to the cecum

aquaporin.meaning: protein-forming water channels through the lipid bilayer of the cell; allows water to cross; activation in the collecting ducts is under the control of ADH

aqueous humour.meaning: watery fluid that fills the anterior chamber containing the cornea, iris, ciliary body, and lens of the eye

arachnoid granulation.meaning: outpocket of the arachnoid membrane into the dural sinuses that allows for reabsorption of CSF into the blood

arachnoid mater.meaning: middle layer of the meninges named for the spider-web–like trabeculae that extend between it and the pia mater

arachnoid trabeculae.meaning: filaments between the arachnoid and pia mater within the subarachnoid space

arcuate line of the ilium.meaning: smooth ridge located at the inferior margin of the iliac fossa; forms the lateral portion of the pelvic brim

areola.meaning: highly pigmented, circular area surrounding the raised nipple and containing areolar glands that secrete fluid important for lubrication during suckling

areolar tissue.meaning: (also, loose connective tissue) a type of connective tissue proper that shows little specialisation with cells dispersed in the matrix

arm.meaning: region of the upper limb located between the shoulder and elbow joints; contains the humerus bone

arrector pili.meaning: smooth muscle that is activated in response to external stimuli that pull on hair follicles and make the hair “stand up”

arterial circle.meaning: (also, circle of Willis) anastomosis located at the base of the brain that ensures continual blood supply; formed from branches of the internal carotid and vertebral arteries; supplies blood to the brain

arteriole.meaning: (also, resistance vessel) very small artery that leads to a capillary

arteriovenous anastomosis.meaning: short vessel connecting an arteriole directly to a venule and bypassing the capillary beds

artery.meaning: blood vessel that conducts blood away from the heart; may be a conducting or distributing vessel

articular capsule.meaning: connective tissue structure that encloses the joint cavity of a synovial joint

articular cartilage.meaning: thin layer of cartilage covering an epiphysis; reduces friction and acts as a shock absorber

articular disc.meaning: meniscus; a fibrocartilage structure found between the bones of some synovial joints; provides padding or smooths movements between the bones; strongly unites the bones together

articular tubercle.meaning: smooth ridge located on the inferior skull, immediately anterior to the mandibular fossa

artificial pacemaker.meaning: medical device that transmits electrical signals to the heart to ensure that it contracts and pumps blood to the body

ascending aorta.meaning: initial portion of the aorta, rising from the left ventricle for a distance of approximately 5 cm

ascending pathway.meaning: fibre structure that relays sensory information from the periphery through the spinal cord and brainstem to other structures of the brain

ascending tract.meaning: central nervous system fibres carrying sensory information from the spinal cord or periphery to the brain

association area.meaning: region of cortex connected to a primary sensory cortical area that further processes the information to generate more complex sensory perceptions

astrocyte.meaning: star-shaped cell in the central nervous system that regulates ions and uptake and/or breakdown of some neurotransmitters and contributes to the formation of the blood-brain barrier

ataxia.meaning: movement disorder related to damage of the cerebellum characterised by loss of coordination in voluntary movements

atlanto-occipital joint.meaning: articulation between the occipital condyles of the skull and the superior articular processes of the atlas (C1 vertebra)

atlantoaxial joint.meaning: series of three articulations between the atlas (C1) vertebra and the axis (C2) vertebra, consisting of the joints between the inferior articular processes of C1 and the superior articular processes of C2, and the articulation between the dens of C2 and the anterior arch of C1

atmospheric pressure.meaning: amount of force that is exerted by gases in the air surrounding any given surface

atom.meaning: smallest unit of an element that retains the unique properties of that element

atomic number.meaning: number of protons in the nucleus of an atom

atp synthase.meaning: protein pore complex that creates ATP

atpase.meaning: enzyme that hydrolyses ATP to ADP

atrial natriuretic peptide.meaning: peptide hormone produced by the walls of the atria in response to high blood pressure, blood volume, or blood sodium that reduces the reabsorption of sodium and water in the kidneys and promotes vasodilation

atrial reflex.meaning: mechanism for maintaining vascular homeostasis involving atrial baroreceptors: if blood is returning to the right atrium more rapidly than it is being ejected from the left ventricle, the atrial receptors will stimulate the cardiovascular centres to increase sympathetic firing and increase cardiac output until the situation is reversed; the opposite is also true

atrioventricular (av) node.meaning: clump of myocardial cells located in the inferior portion of the right atrium within the atrioventricular septum; receives the impulse from the SA node, pauses, and then transmits it into specialised conducting cells within the interventricular septum

atrioventricular bundle.meaning: (also, bundle of His) group of specialised myocardial conductile cells that transmit the impulse from the AV node through the interventricular septum; form the left and right atrioventricular bundle branches

atrioventricular bundle branches.meaning: (also, left or right bundle branches) specialised myocardial conductile cells that arise from the bifurcation of the atrioventricular bundle and pass through the interventricular septum; lead to the Purkinje fibres and also to the right papillary muscle via the moderator band

atrioventricular septum.meaning: cardiac septum located between the atria and ventricles; atrioventricular valves are located here

atrioventricular valves.meaning: one-way valves located between the atria and ventricles; the valve on the right is called the tricuspid valve, and the one on the left is the mitral or bicuspid valve

atrium.meaning: (plural = atria) upper or receiving chamber of the heart that pumps blood into the lower chambers just prior to their contraction; the right atrium receives blood from the systemic circuit that flows into the right ventricle; the left atrium receives blood from the pulmonary circuit that flows into the left ventricle

auricle.meaning: fleshy external structure of the ear

auricular surface of the ilium.meaning: roughened area located on the posterior, medial side of the ilium of the hip bone; articulates with the auricular surface of the sacrum to form the sacroiliac joint

autocrine.meaning: chemical signal that elicits a response in the same cell that secreted it

autolysis.meaning: breakdown of cells by their own enzymatic action

autonomic nervous system.meaning: functional division of the nervous system that is responsible for homeostatic reflexes that coordinate control of cardiac and smooth muscle, as well as glandular tissue

autonomic tone.meaning: tendency of an organ system to be governed by one division of the autonomic nervous system over the other, such as heart rate being lowered by parasympathetic input at rest

autophagy.meaning: lysosomal breakdown of a cell’s own components

autorhythmicity.meaning: heart’s ability to control its own contractions

autosomal chromosome.meaning: in humans, the 22 pairs of chromosomes that are not the sex chromosomes (XX or XY)

autosomal dominant.meaning: pattern of dominant inheritance that corresponds to a gene on one of the 22 autosomal chromosomes

autosomal recessive.meaning: pattern of recessive inheritance that corresponds to a gene on one of the 22 autosomal chromosomes

axial skeleton.meaning: central, vertical axis of the body, including the skull, vertebral column, and thoracic cage

axillary artery.meaning: continuation of the subclavian artery as it penetrates the body wall and enters the axillary region; supplies blood to the region near the head of the humerus (humeral circumflex arteries); the majority of the vessel continues into the brachium and becomes the brachial artery

axillary nerve.meaning: systemic nerve of the arm that arises from the brachial plexus

axillary vein.meaning: major vein in the axillary region; drains the upper limb and becomes the subclavian vein

axon.meaning: single process of the neuron that carries an electrical signal (action potential) away from the cell body toward a target cell

axon hillock.meaning: tapering of the neuron cell body that gives rise to the axon

axon segment.meaning: single stretch of the axon insulated by myelin and bounded by nodes of Ranvier at either end (except for the first, which is after the initial segment, and the last, which is followed by the axon terminal)

axon terminal.meaning: end of the axon, where there are usually several branches extending toward the target cell

axoplasm.meaning: cytoplasm of an axon, which is different in composition than the cytoplasm of the neuronal cell body

azygos vein.meaning: originates in the lumbar region and passes through the diaphragm into the thoracic cavity on the right side of the vertebral column; drains blood from the intercostal veins, esophageal veins, bronchial veins, and other veins draining the mediastinal region; leads to the superior vena cava

b cells.meaning: lymphocytes that act by differentiating into an antibody-secreting plasma cell

b lymphocytes.meaning: (also, B cells) lymphocytes that defend the body against specific pathogens and thereby provide specific immunity

babinski sign.meaning: dorsiflexion of the foot with extension and splaying of the toes in response to the plantar reflex, normally suppressed by corticospinal input

bachmann’s bundle.meaning: (also, interatrial band) group of specialised conducting cells that transmit the impulse directly from the SA node in the right atrium to the left atrium

bainbridge reflex.meaning: (also, called atrial reflex) autonomic reflex that responds to stretch receptors in the atria that send impulses to the cardioaccelerator area to increase HR when venous flow into the atria increases

ball-and-socket joint.meaning: synovial joint formed between the spherical end of one bone (the ball) that fits into the depression of a second bone (the socket); found at the hip and shoulder joints; functionally classified as a multiaxial joint

baroreceptor.meaning: mechanoreceptor that senses the stretch of blood vessels to indicate changes in blood pressure

baroreceptor reflex.meaning: autonomic reflex in which the cardiac centres monitor signals from the baroreceptor stretch receptors and regulate heart function based on blood flow

barrier defences.meaning: antipathogen defences deriving from a barrier that physically prevents pathogens from entering the body to establish an infection

bartholin’s glands.meaning: (also, greater vestibular glands) glands that produce a thick mucus that maintains moisture in the vulva area; also referred to as the greater vestibular glands

basal cell.meaning: type of stem cell found in the stratum basale and in the hair matrix that continually undergoes cell division, producing the keratinocytes of the epidermis

basal cell carcinoma.meaning: cancer that originates from basal cells in the epidermis of the skin

basal forebrain.meaning: nuclei of the cerebrum related to modulation of sensory stimuli and attention through broad projections to the cerebral cortex, loss of which is related to Alzheimer’s disease

basal lamina.meaning: thin extracellular layer that lies underneath epithelial cells and separates them from other tissues

basal metabolic rate.meaning: amount of energy expended by the body at rest

basal nuclei.meaning: nuclei of the cerebrum (with a few components in the upper brainstem and diencephalon) that are responsible for assessing cortical movement commands and comparing them with the general state of the individual through broad modulatory activity of dopamine neurons; largely related to motor functions, as evidenced through the symptoms of Parkinson’s and Huntington’s diseases

basal plate.meaning: developmental region of the spinal cord that gives rise to the lateral and anterior horns of grey matter

base.meaning: compound that accepts hydrogen ions (H+) in solution

base of the metatarsal bone.meaning: expanded, proximal end of each metatarsal bone

basement membrane.meaning: in epithelial tissue, a thin layer of fibrous material that anchors the epithelial tissue to the underlying connective tissue; made up of the basal lamina and reticular lamina

basilar artery.meaning: formed from the fusion of the two vertebral arteries; sends branches to the cerebellum, brainstem, and the posterior cerebral arteries; the main blood supply to the brainstem

basilar membrane.meaning: in the ear, the floor of the cochlear duct on which the organ of Corti sits

basilic vein.meaning: superficial vein of the arm that arises from the palmar venous arches, intersects with the median cubital vein, parallels the ulnar vein, and continues into the upper arm; along with the brachial vein, it leads to the axillary vein

basophils.meaning: granulocytes that stain with a basic (alkaline) stain and store histamine and heparin

bedsore.meaning: sore on the skin that develops when regions of the body start necrotising due to constant pressure and lack of blood supply; also called decubitus ulcers

belly.meaning: bulky central body of a muscle

beta (β)-adrenergic receptor.meaning: one of the receptors to which epinephrine and norepinephrine bind, which comes in three subtypes: β1, β2, and β3

beta (β)-hydroxybutyrate.meaning: primary ketone body produced in the body

beta cell.meaning: pancreatic islet cell type that produces the hormone insulin

betz cells.meaning: output cells of the primary motor cortex that cause musculature to move through synapses on cranial and spinal motor neurons

biaxial joint.meaning: type of diarthrosis; a joint that allows for movements within two planes (two axes)

biceps brachii.meaning: two-headed muscle that crosses the shoulder and elbow joints to flex the forearm while assisting in supinating it and flexing the arm at the shoulder

bicipital groove.meaning: intertubercular groove; narrow groove located between the greater and lesser tubercles of the humerus

bicuspid valve.meaning: (also, mitral valve or left atrioventricular valve) valve located between the left atrium and ventricle; consists of two flaps of tissue

bile.meaning: alkaline solution produced by the liver and important for the emulsification of lipids

bile canaliculus.meaning: small duct between hepatocytes that collects bile

bile salts.meaning: salts that are released from the liver in response to lipid ingestion and surround the insoluble triglycerides to aid in their conversion to monoglycerides and free fatty acids

bilirubin.meaning: main bile pigment, which is responsible for the brown colour of faeces

biliverdin.meaning: green bile pigment produced when the non-iron portion of heme is degraded into a waste product; converted to bilirubin in the liver

binocular depth cues.meaning: indications of the distance of visual stimuli on the basis of slight differences in the images projected onto either retina

biogenic amine.meaning: class of neurotransmitters that are enzymatically derived from amino acids but no longer contain a carboxyl group

biosynthesis reactions.meaning: reactions that create new molecules, also called anabolic reactions

bipennate.meaning: pennate muscle that has fascicles that are located on both sides of the tendon

bipolar.meaning: shape of a neuron with two processes extending from the neuron cell body—the axon and one dendrite

bipolar cell.meaning: cell type in the retina that connects the photoreceptors to the RGCs

blastocyst.meaning: term for the conceptus at the developmental stage that consists of about 100 cells shaped into an inner cell mass that is fated to become the embryo and an outer trophoblast that is fated to become the associated fetal membranes and placenta

blood.meaning: liquid connective tissue composed of formed elements—erythrocytes, leukocytes, and platelets—and a fluid extracellular matrix called plasma; component of the cardiovascular system

blood colloidal osmotic pressure.meaning: pressure exerted by colloids suspended in blood within a vessel; a primary determinant is the presence of plasma proteins

blood flow.meaning: movement of blood through a vessel, tissue, or organ that is usually expressed in terms of volume per unit of time

blood hydrostatic pressure.meaning: force blood exerts against the walls of a blood vessel or heart chamber

blood islands.meaning: masses of developing blood vessels and formed elements from mesodermal cells scattered throughout the embryonic disc

blood pressure.meaning: force exerted by the blood against the wall of a vessel or heart chamber; can be described with the more generic term hydrostatic pressure

blood-brain barrier.meaning: physiological barrier between the circulatory system and the central nervous system that establishes a privileged blood supply, restricting the flow of substances into the CNS

blood–testis barrier.meaning: tight junctions between Sertoli cells that prevent bloodborne pathogens from gaining access to later stages of spermatogenesis and prevent the potential for an autoimmune reaction to haploid sperm

body mass index.meaning: relative amount of body weight compared to the overall height; a BMI ranging from 18–24.9 is considered normal weight, 25–29.9 is considered overweight, and greater than 30 is considered obese

bohr effect.meaning: relationship between blood pH and oxygen dissociation from haemoglobin

bone.meaning: hard, dense connective tissue that forms the structural elements of the skeleton

bone marrow.meaning: tissue found inside bones; the site of all blood cell differentiation and maturation of B lymphocytes

bone marrow biopsy.meaning: diagnostic test of a sample of red bone marrow

bone marrow transplant.meaning: treatment in which a donor’s healthy bone marrow with its stem cells replaces diseased or damaged bone marrow of a patient

bowman’s capsule.meaning: cup-shaped sack lined by a simple squamous epithelium (parietal surface) and specialised cells called podocytes (visceral surface) that participate in the filtration process; receives the filtrate which then passes on to the PCTs

boyle’s law.meaning: relationship between volume and pressure as described by the formula: P1V1 = P2V2

brachial artery.meaning: continuation of the axillary artery in the brachium; supplies blood to much of the brachial region; gives off several smaller branches that provide blood to the posterior surface of the arm in the region of the elbow; bifurcates into the radial and ulnar arteries at the coronoid fossa

brachial plexus.meaning: nerve plexus associated with the lower cervical spinal nerves and first thoracic spinal nerve

brachial vein.meaning: deeper vein of the arm that forms from the radial and ulnar veins in the lower arm; leads to the axillary vein

brachialis.meaning: muscle deep to the biceps brachii that provides power in flexing the forearm.

brachiocephalic artery.meaning: single vessel located on the right side of the body; the first vessel branching from the aortic arch; gives rise to the right subclavian artery and the right common carotid artery; supplies blood to the head, neck, upper limb, and wall of the thoracic region

brachiocephalic vein.meaning: one of a pair of veins that form from a fusion of the external and internal jugular veins and the subclavian vein; subclavian, external and internal jugulars, vertebral, and internal thoracic veins lead to it; drains the upper thoracic region and flows into the superior vena cava

brachioradialis.meaning: muscle that can flex the forearm quickly or help lift a load slowly

brain.meaning: the large organ of the central nervous system composed of white and grey matter, contained within the cranium and continuous with the spinal cord

brain case.meaning: portion of the skull that contains and protects the brain, consisting of the eight bones that form the cranial base and rounded upper skull

brainstem.meaning: region of the adult brain that includes the midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata and develops from the mesencephalon, metencephalon, and myelencephalon of the embryonic brain

braxton hicks contractions.meaning: weak and irregular peristaltic contractions that can occur in the second and third trimesters; they do not indicate that childbirth is imminent

bridge.meaning: portion of the external nose that lies in the area of the nasal bones

broad ligament.meaning: wide ligament that supports the uterus by attaching laterally to both sides of the uterus and pelvic wall

broca’s area.meaning: region of the frontal lobe associated with the motor commands necessary for speech production and located only in the cerebral hemisphere responsible for language production, which is the left side in approximately 95 percent of the population

brodmann’s areas.meaning: mapping of regions of the cerebral cortex based on microscopic anatomy that relates specific areas to functional differences, as described by Brodmann in the early 1900s

bronchial artery.meaning: systemic branch from the aorta that provides oxygenated blood to the lungs in addition to the pulmonary circuit

bronchial bud.meaning: structure in the developing embryo that forms when the laryngotracheal bud extends and branches to form two bulbous structures

bronchial tree.meaning: collective name for the multiple branches of the bronchi and bronchioles of the respiratory system

bronchial vein.meaning: drains the systemic circulation from the lungs and leads to the azygos vein

bronchiole.meaning: branch of bronchi that are 1 mm or less in diameter and terminate at alveolar sacs

bronchoconstriction.meaning: decrease in the size of the bronchiole due to contraction of the muscular wall

bronchodilation.meaning: increase in the size of the bronchiole due to relaxation of the muscular wall

bronchus.meaning: tube connected to the trachea that branches into many subsidiaries and provides a passageway for air to enter and leave the lungs

bronchus-associated lymphoid tissue.meaning: lymphoid nodule associated with the respiratory tract

brown adipose tissue.meaning: highly vascularised fat tissue that is packed with mitochondria; these properties confer the ability to oxidise fatty acids to generate heat

bruise.meaning: localised bleeding under the skin due to damaged blood vessels

brush border.meaning: formed by microvilli on the surface of certain cuboidal cells; in the kidney it is found in the PCT; increases surface area for absorption in the kidney

buffer.meaning: solution containing a weak acid or a weak base that opposes wide fluctuations in the pH of body fluids

buffy coat.meaning: thin, pale layer of leukocytes and platelets that separates the erythrocytes from the plasma in a sample of centrifuged blood

bulbourethral glands.meaning: (also, Cowper’s glands) glands that secrete a lubricating mucus that cleans and lubricates the urethra prior to and during ejaculation

bulbus cordis.meaning: portion of the primitive heart tube that will eventually develop into the right ventricle

bundle of his.meaning: (also, atrioventricular bundle) group of specialised myocardial conductile cells that transmit the impulse from the AV node through the interventricular septum; form the left and right atrioventricular bundle branches

bursa.meaning: connective tissue sac containing lubricating fluid that prevents friction between adjacent structures, such as skin and bone, tendons and bone, or between muscles

calcaneal tendon.meaning: (also, Achilles tendon) strong tendon that inserts into the calcaneal bone of the ankle

calcaneofibular ligament.meaning: intrinsic ligament located on the lateral side of the ankle joint, between the calcaneus bone and lateral malleolus of the fibula; supports the talus bone at the ankle joint and resists excess inversion of the foot

calcaneus.meaning: heel bone; posterior, inferior tarsal bone that forms the heel of the foot

calcitonin.meaning: peptide hormone produced and secreted by the parafollicular cells (C cells) of the thyroid gland that functions to decrease blood calcium levels

callus.meaning: thickened area of skin that arises due to constant abrasion

calmodulin.meaning: regulatory protein that facilitates contraction in smooth muscles

calorie.meaning: amount of heat it takes to raise 1 kg (1000 g) of water by 1 °C

calvaria.meaning: (also, skullcap) rounded top of the skull

calyces.meaning: cup-like structures receiving urine from the collecting ducts where it passes on to the renal pelvis and ureter

canaliculi.meaning: (singular = canaliculus) channels within the bone matrix that house one of an osteocyte’s many cytoplasmic extensions that it uses to communicate and receive nutrients

capacitance.meaning: ability of a vein to distend and store blood

capacitation.meaning: process that occurs in the female reproductive tract in which sperm are prepared for fertilisation; leads to increased motility and changes in their outer membrane that improve their ability to release enzymes capable of digesting an oocyte’s outer layers

capillary.meaning: smallest of blood vessels where physical exchange occurs between the blood and tissue cells surrounded by interstitial fluid

capillary bed.meaning: network of 10–100 capillaries connecting arterioles to venules

capillary hydrostatic pressure.meaning: force blood exerts against a capillary

capitate.meaning: from the lateral side, the third of the four distal carpal bones; articulates with the scaphoid and lunate proximally, the trapezoid laterally, the hamate medially, and primarily with the third metacarpal distally

capitulum.meaning: knob-like bony structure located anteriorly on the lateral, distal end of the humerus

capsaicin.meaning: molecule that activates nociceptors by interacting with a temperature-sensitive ion channel and is the basis for “hot” sensations in spicy food

carbaminohemoglobin.meaning: bound form of haemoglobin and carbon dioxide

carbohydrate.meaning: class of organic compounds built from sugars, molecules containing carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen in a 1-2-1 ratio

carbonic anhydrase.meaning: enzyme that catalyses the reaction that causes carbon dioxide and water to form carbonic acid

cardia.meaning: (also, cardiac region) part of the stomach surrounding the cardiac orifice (esophageal hiatus)

cardiac accelerator nerves.meaning: preganglionic sympathetic fibres that cause the heart rate to increase when the cardiovascular centre in the medulla initiates a signal

cardiac cycle.meaning: period of time between the onset of atrial contraction (atrial systole) and ventricular relaxation (ventricular diastole)

cardiac muscle.meaning: heart muscle, under involuntary control, composed of striated cells that attach to form fibres, each cell contains a single nucleus, contracts autonomously

cardiac notch.meaning: indentation on the surface of the left lung that allows space for the heart

cardiac output.meaning: amount of blood pumped by each ventricle during one minute; equals HR multiplied by SV

cardiac plexus.meaning: paired complex network of nerve fibres near the base of the heart that receive sympathetic and parasympathetic stimulations to regulate HR

cardiac reflexes.meaning: series of autonomic reflexes that enable the cardiovascular centres to regulate heart function based upon sensory information from a variety of visceral sensors

cardiac reserve.meaning: difference between maximum and resting CO

cardiac skeleton.meaning: (also, skeleton of the heart) reinforced connective tissue located within the atrioventricular septum; includes four rings that surround the openings between the atria and ventricles, and the openings to the pulmonary trunk and aorta; the point of attachment for the heart valves

cardiogenic area.meaning: area near the head of the embryo where the heart begins to develop 18–19 days after fertilisation

cardiogenic cords.meaning: two strands of tissue that form within the cardiogenic area

cardiogenic shock.meaning: type of shock that results from the inability of the heart to maintain cardiac output

cardiovascular centre.meaning: region in the medulla that controls the cardiovascular system through cardiac accelerator nerves and vasomotor nerves, which are components of the sympathetic division of the autonomic nervous system

carotid canal.meaning: zigzag tunnel providing passage through the base of the skull for the internal carotid artery to the brain; begins anteromedial to the styloid process and terminates in the middle cranial cavity, near the posterior-lateral base of the sella turcica

carotid sinuses.meaning: small pockets near the base of the internal carotid arteries that are the locations of the baroreceptors and chemoreceptors that trigger a reflex that aids in the regulation of vascular homeostasis

carpal bone.meaning: one of the eight small bones that form the wrist and base of the hand; these are grouped as a proximal row consisting of (from lateral to medial) the scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, and pisiform bones, and a distal row containing (from lateral to medial) the trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, and hamate bones

carpal tunnel.meaning: passageway between the anterior forearm and hand formed by the carpal bones and flexor retinaculum

carpometacarpal joint.meaning: articulation between one of the carpal bones in the distal row and a metacarpal bone of the hand

carrier.meaning: heterozygous individual who does not display symptoms of a recessive genetic disorder but can transmit the disorder to their offspring

cartilage.meaning: semi-rigid connective tissue found on the skeleton in areas where flexibility and smooth surfaces support movement

cartilaginous joint.meaning: joint at which the bones are united by hyaline cartilage (synchondrosis) or fibrocartilage (symphysis)

catabolic hormones.meaning: hormones that stimulate the breakdown of larger molecules

catabolic reactions.meaning: reactions that break down larger molecules into their constituent parts

catabolism.meaning: breaking down of more complex molecules into simpler molecules

catagen.meaning: transitional phase marking the end of the anagen phase of the hair growth cycle

catalyst.meaning: substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself being changed in the process

cauda equina.meaning: bundle of spinal nerve roots that descend from the lower spinal cord below the first lumbar vertebra and lie within the vertebral cavity; has the appearance of a horse's tail

caudal.meaning: describes a position below or lower than another part of the body proper; near or toward the tail (in humans, the coccyx, or lowest part of the spinal column); also referred to as inferior

caudate.meaning: nucleus deep in the cerebrum that is part of the basal nuclei; along with the putamen, it is part of the striatum

caval opening.meaning: opening in the diaphragm that allows the inferior vena cava to pass through; foramen for the vena cava

cavernous sinus.meaning: enlarged vein that receives blood from most of the other cerebral veins and the eye socket, and leads to the petrosal sinus

cecum.meaning: pouch forming the beginning of the large intestine

celiac ganglion.meaning: one of the collateral ganglia of the sympathetic system that projects to the digestive system

celiac trunk.meaning: (also, celiac artery) major branch of the abdominal aorta; gives rise to the left gastric artery, the splenic artery, and the common hepatic artery that forms the hepatic artery to the liver, the right gastric artery to the stomach, and the cystic artery to the gall bladder

cell.meaning: smallest independently functioning unit of all organisms; in animals, a cell contains cytoplasm, composed of fluid and organelles

cell cycle.meaning: life cycle of a single cell, from its birth until its division into two new daughter cells

cell junction.meaning: point of cell-to-cell contact that connects one cell to another in a tissue

cell membrane.meaning: membrane surrounding all animal cells, composed of a lipid bilayer interspersed with various molecules; also known as plasma membrane

cellular respiration.meaning: production of ATP from glucose oxidation via glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation

cementum.meaning: bone-like tissue covering the root of a tooth

central canal.meaning: longitudinal channel in the centre of each osteon; contains blood vessels, nerves, and lymphatic vessels; also known as the Haversian canal

central chemoreceptor.meaning: one of the specialised receptors that are located in the brain that sense changes in hydrogen ion, oxygen, or carbon dioxide concentrations in the brain

central nervous system.meaning: anatomical division of the nervous system located within the cranial and vertebral cavities, namely the brain and spinal cord

central neuron.meaning: specifically referring to the cell body of a neuron in the autonomic system that is located in the central nervous system, specifically the lateral horn of the spinal cord or a brainstem nucleus

central sulcus.meaning: surface landmark of the cerebral cortex that marks the boundary between the frontal and parietal lobes

central tolerance.meaning: B cell tolerance induced in immature B cells of the bone marrow

central vein.meaning: vein that receives blood from hepatic sinusoids

centriole.meaning: small, self-replicating organelle that provides the origin for microtubule growth and moves DNA during cell division

centromere.meaning: region of attachment for two sister chromatids

centrosome.meaning: cellular structure that organises microtubules during cell division

cephalic flexure.meaning: curve in midbrain of the embryo that positions the forebrain ventrally

cephalic phase.meaning: (also, reflex phase) initial phase of gastric secretion that occurs before food enters the stomach

cephalic vein.meaning: superficial vessel in the upper arm; leads to the axillary vein

cerebellum.meaning: region of the adult brain connected primarily to the pons that developed from the metencephalon (along with the pons) and is largely responsible for comparing information from the cerebrum with sensory feedback from the periphery through the spinal cord

cerebral aqueduct.meaning: connection of the ventricular system between the third and fourth ventricles located in the midbrain

cerebral cortex.meaning: outermost layer of grey matter in the brain, where conscious perception takes place

cerebral hemisphere.meaning: one half of the bilaterally symmetrical cerebrum

cerebral peduncles.meaning: segments of the descending motor pathway that make up the white matter of the ventral midbrain

cerebrocerebellum.meaning: lateral regions of the cerebellum; named for the significant input from the cerebral cortex

cerebrospinal fluid.meaning: circulatory medium within the CNS that is produced by ependymal cells in the choroid plexus filtering the blood

cerebrovascular accident.meaning: blockage of blood flow to the brain; also called a stroke

cerebrum.meaning: region of the adult brain that develops from the telencephalon and is responsible for higher neurological functions such as memory, emotion, and consciousness

cervical curve.meaning: posteriorly concave curvature of the cervical vertebral column region; a secondary curve of the vertebral column

cervical enlargement.meaning: region of the ventral (anterior) horn of the spinal cord that has a larger population of motor neurons for the greater number of and finer control of muscles of the upper limb

cervical plexus.meaning: nerve plexus associated with the upper cervical spinal nerves

cervical vertebrae.meaning: seven vertebrae numbered as C1–C7 that are located in the neck region of the vertebral column

cervix.meaning: elongate inferior end of the uterus where it connects to the vagina

channel protein.meaning: membrane-spanning protein that has an inner pore which allows the passage of one or more substances

check reflex.meaning: response to a release in resistance so that the contractions stop, or check, movement

checkpoint.meaning: progress point in the cell cycle during which certain conditions must be met in order for the cell to proceed to a subsequence phase

chemical energy.meaning: form of energy that is absorbed as chemical bonds form, stored as they are maintained, and released as they are broken

chemical synapse.meaning: connection between two neurons, or between a neuron and its target, where a neurotransmitter diffuses across a very short distance

chemoreceptor.meaning: sensory receptor cell that is sensitive to chemical stimuli, such as in taste, smell, or pain

chief cell.meaning: gastric gland cell that secretes pepsinogen

chief sensory nucleus.meaning: component of the trigeminal nuclei that is found in the pons

chloride shift.meaning: facilitated diffusion that exchanges bicarbonate (HCO3–) with chloride (Cl–) ions

cholecystokinin.meaning: hormone that stimulates the release of pancreatic lipase and the contraction of the gallbladder to release bile salts

cholinergic.meaning: synapse at which acetylcholine is released and binds to the nicotinic or muscarinic receptor

cholinergic system.meaning: neurotransmitter system of acetylcholine, which includes its receptors and the enzyme acetylcholinesterase

chordae tendineae.meaning: string-like extensions of tough connective tissue that extend from the flaps of the atrioventricular valves to the papillary muscles

chorion.meaning: membrane that develops from the syncytiotrophoblast, cytotrophoblast, and mesoderm; surrounds the embryo and forms the fetal portion of the placenta through the chorionic villi

chorionic membrane.meaning: precursor to the chorion; forms from extra-embryonic mesoderm cells

chorionic villi.meaning: projections of the chorionic membrane that burrow into the endometrium and develop into the placenta

choroid.meaning: highly vascular tissue in the wall of the eye that supplies the outer retina with blood

choroid plexus.meaning: specialised structure containing ependymal cells that line blood capillaries and filter blood to produce CSF in the four ventricles of the brain

chromaffin.meaning: neuroendocrine cells of the adrenal medulla

chromaffin cells.meaning: neuroendocrine cells of the adrenal medulla that release epinephrine and norepinephrine into the bloodstream as part of sympathetic system activity

chromatin.meaning: substance consisting of DNA and associated proteins

chronic inflammation.meaning: inflammation occurring for long periods of time

chyle.meaning: lipid-rich lymph inside the lymphatic capillaries of the small intestine

chylomicron.meaning: large lipid-transport compound made up of triglycerides, phospholipids, cholesterol, and proteins

chylomicrons.meaning: vesicles containing cholesterol and triglycerides that transport lipids out of the intestinal cells and into the lymphatic and circulatory systems

chyme.meaning: soupy liquid created when food is mixed with digestive juices

chymotrypsinogen.meaning: proenzyme that is activated by trypsin into chymotrypsin

cilia.meaning: small appendage on certain cells formed by microtubules and modified for movement of materials across the cellular surface

ciliary body.meaning: smooth muscle structure on the interior surface of the iris that controls the shape of the lens through the zonule fibres

ciliary ganglion.meaning: one of the terminal ganglia of the parasympathetic system, located in the posterior orbit, axons from which project to the iris

circadian rhythm.meaning: internal perception of the daily cycle of light and dark based on retinal activity related to sunlight

circle of willis.meaning: (also, arterial circle) anastomosis located at the base of the brain that ensures continual blood supply; formed from branches of the internal carotid and vertebral arteries; supplies blood to the brain

circular.meaning: (also, sphincter) fascicles that are concentrically arranged around an opening

circular fold.meaning: (also, plica circulare) deep fold in the mucosa and submucosa of the small intestine

circulatory shock.meaning: also simply called shock; a life-threatening medical condition in which the circulatory system is unable to supply enough blood flow to provide adequate oxygen and other nutrients to the tissues to maintain cellular metabolism

circumduction.meaning: circular motion of the arm, thigh, hand, thumb, or finger that is produced by the sequential combination of flexion, abduction, extension, and adduction

circumflex artery.meaning: branch of the left coronary artery that follows coronary sulcus

cisterna chyli.meaning: bag-like vessel that forms the beginning of the thoracic duct

citric acid cycle.meaning: also called the Krebs cycle or the tricarboxylic acid cycle; converts pyruvate into CO2 and high-energy FADH2, NADH, and ATP molecules

clasp-knife response.meaning: sign of UMN disease when a patient initially resists passive movement of a muscle but will quickly release to a lower state of resistance

class switching.meaning: ability of B cells to change the class of antibody they produce without altering the specificity for antigen

clavicle.meaning: collarbone; elongated bone that articulates with the manubrium of the sternum medially and the acromion of the scapula laterally

clavicular notch.meaning: paired notches located on the superior-lateral sides of the sternal manubrium, for articulation with the clavicle

cleavage.meaning: form of mitotic cell division in which the cell divides but the total volume remains unchanged; this process serves to produce smaller and smaller cells

cleavage furrow.meaning: contractile ring that forms around a cell during cytokinesis that pinches the cell into two halves

clitoris.meaning: (also, glans clitoris) nerve-rich area of the vulva that contributes to sexual sensation during intercourse

clonal anergy.meaning: process whereby B cells that react to soluble antigens in bone marrow are made nonfunctional

clonal deletion.meaning: removal of self-reactive B cells by inducing apoptosis

clonal expansion.meaning: growth of a clone of selected lymphocytes

clonal selection.meaning: stimulating growth of lymphocytes that have specific receptors

clone.meaning: group of lymphocytes sharing the same antigen receptor

closed reduction.meaning: manual manipulation of a broken bone to set it into its natural position without surgery

clotting.meaning: also called coagulation; complex process by which blood components form a plug to stop bleeding

clotting factors.meaning: group of 12 identified substances active in coagulation

coagulation.meaning: formation of a blood clot; part of the process of haemostasis

coccyx.meaning: small bone located at inferior end of the adult vertebral column that is formed by the fusion of four coccygeal vertebrae; also referred to as the “tailbone”

cochlea.meaning: auditory portion of the inner ear containing structures to transduce sound stimuli

cochlear duct.meaning: space within the auditory portion of the inner ear that contains the organ of Corti and is adjacent to the scala tympani and scala vestibuli on either side

codominance.meaning: pattern of inheritance that corresponds to the equal, distinct, and simultaneous expression of two different alleles

codon.meaning: consecutive sequence of three nucleotides on an mRNA molecule that corresponds to a specific amino acid

collagen fibre.meaning: flexible fibrous proteins that give connective tissue tensile strength

collateral ganglia.meaning: ganglia outside of the sympathetic chain that are targets of sympathetic preganglionic fibres, which are the celiac, inferior mesenteric, and superior mesenteric ganglia

colloid.meaning: liquid mixture in which the solute particles consist of clumps of molecules large enough to scatter light

colon.meaning: part of the large intestine between the cecum and the rectum

colony-stimulating factors.meaning: glycoproteins that trigger the proliferation and differentiation of myeloblasts into granular leukocytes (basophils, neutrophils, and eosinophils)

colostrum.meaning: thick, yellowish substance secreted from a mother’s breasts in the first postpartum days; rich in immunoglobulins

common bile duct.meaning: structure formed by the union of the common hepatic duct and the gallbladder’s cystic duct

common carotid artery.meaning: right common carotid artery arises from the brachiocephalic artery, and the left common carotid arises from the aortic arch; gives rise to the external and internal carotid arteries; supplies the respective sides of the head and neck

common hepatic artery.meaning: branch of the celiac trunk that forms the hepatic artery, the right gastric artery, and the cystic artery

common hepatic duct.meaning: duct formed by the merger of the two hepatic ducts

common iliac artery.meaning: branch of the aorta that leads to the internal and external iliac arteries

common iliac vein.meaning: one of a pair of veins that flows into the inferior vena cava at the level of L5; the left common iliac vein drains the sacral region; divides into external and internal iliac veins near the inferior portion of the sacroiliac joint

common pathway.meaning: final coagulation pathway activated either by the intrinsic or the extrinsic pathway, and ending in the formation of a blood clot

compact bone.meaning: dense osseous tissue that can withstand compressive forces

complement.meaning: enzymatic cascade of constitutive blood proteins that have antipathogen effects, including the direct killing of bacteria

compliance.meaning: degree to which a blood vessel can stretch as opposed to being rigid

compound.meaning: substance composed of two or more different elements joined by chemical bonds

computed tomography.meaning: medical imaging technique in which a computer-enhanced cross-sectional X-ray image is obtained

concentration.meaning: number of particles within a given space

concentration gradient.meaning: difference in the concentration of a substance between two regions

concentric contraction.meaning: muscle contraction that shortens the muscle to move a load

conceptus.meaning: pre-implantation stage of a fertilised egg and its associated membranes

conducting zone.meaning: region of the respiratory system that includes the organs and structures that provide passageways for air and are not directly involved in gas exchange

conduction.meaning: transfer of heat through physical contact

conduction aphasia.meaning: loss of language function related to connecting the understanding of speech with the production of speech, without either specific function being lost

conductive hearing.meaning: hearing dependent on the conduction of vibrations of the tympanic membrane through the ossicles of the middle ear

condylar process of the mandible.meaning: thickened upward projection from posterior margin of mandibular ramus

condyle.meaning: oval-shaped process located at the top of the condylar process of the mandible

condyloid joint.meaning: synovial joint in which the shallow depression at the end of one bone receives a rounded end from a second bone or a rounded structure formed by two bones; found at the metacarpophalangeal joints of the fingers or the radiocarpal joint of the wrist; functionally classified as a biaxial joint

cone photoreceptor.meaning: one of the two types of retinal receptor cell that is specialised for colour vision through the use of three photopigments distributed through three separate populations of cells

conjugate gaze.meaning: coordinated movement of the two eyes simultaneously in the same direction

connective tissue.meaning: type of tissue that serves to hold in place, connect, and integrate the body’s organs and systems

connective tissue membrane.meaning: connective tissue that encapsulates organs and lines movable joints

connective tissue proper.meaning: connective tissue containing a viscous matrix, fibres, and cells.

constant region domain.meaning: part of a lymphocyte antigen receptor that does not vary much between different receptor types

continuous capillary.meaning: most common type of capillary, found in virtually all tissues except epithelia and cartilage; contains very small gaps in the endothelial lining that permit exchange

continuous conduction.meaning: slow propagation of an action potential along an unmyelinated axon owing to voltage-gated Na+ channels located along the entire length of the cell membrane

contraction phase.meaning: twitch contraction phase when tension increases

contralateral.meaning: word meaning “on the opposite side,” as in axons that cross the midline in a fibre tract

control centre.meaning: compares values to their normal range; deviations cause the activation of an effector

convection.meaning: transfer of heat between the skin and air or water

convergence.meaning: in vision, the movement of the eyes so that they are both pointed at the same point in space, which increases for stimuli that are closer to the subject

convergent.meaning: fascicles that extend over a broad area and converge on a common attachment site

coordination exam.meaning: major section of the neurological exam that assesses complex, coordinated motor functions of the cerebellum and associated motor pathways

coracobrachialis.meaning: muscle that flexes and adducts the arm

coracoclavicular ligament.meaning: strong band of connective tissue that anchors the coracoid process of the scapula to the lateral clavicle; provides important indirect support for the acromioclavicular joint

coracohumeral ligament.meaning: intrinsic ligament of the shoulder joint; runs from the coracoid process of the scapula to the anterior humerus

coracoid process.meaning: short, hook-like process that projects anteriorly and laterally from the superior margin of the scapula

corn.meaning: type of callus that is named for its shape and the elliptical motion of the abrasive force

cornea.meaning: fibrous covering of the anterior region of the eye that is transparent so that light can pass through it

corneal reflex.meaning: protective response to stimulation of the cornea causing contraction of the orbicularis oculi muscle resulting in blinking of the eye

corona radiata.meaning: in an oocyte, a layer of granulosa cells that surrounds the oocyte and that must be penetrated by sperm before fertilisation can occur

coronal suture.meaning: joint that unites the frontal bone to the right and left parietal bones across the top of the skull

coronary arteries.meaning: branches of the ascending aorta that supply blood to the heart; the left coronary artery feeds the left side of the heart, the left atrium and ventricle, and the interventricular septum; the right coronary artery feeds the right atrium, portions of both ventricles, and the heart conduction system

coronary sinus.meaning: large, thin-walled vein on the posterior surface of the heart that lies within the atrioventricular sulcus and drains the heart myocardium directly into the right atrium

coronary sulcus.meaning: sulcus that marks the boundary between the atria and ventricles

coronary veins.meaning: vessels that drain the heart and generally parallel the large surface arteries

coronoid fossa.meaning: depression on the anterior surface of the humerus above the trochlea; this space receives the coronoid process of the ulna when the elbow is maximally flexed

coronoid process of the mandible.meaning: flattened upward projection from the anterior margin of the mandibular ramus

coronoid process of the ulna.meaning: projecting bony lip located on the anterior, proximal ulna; forms the inferior margin of the trochlear notch

corpus albicans.meaning: nonfunctional structure remaining in the ovarian stroma following structural and functional regression of the corpus luteum

corpus callosum.meaning: large white matter structure that connects the right and left cerebral hemispheres

corpus cavernosum.meaning: (plural = corpora cavernosa) either of two columns of erectile tissue in the penis that fill with blood during an erection

corpus luteum.meaning: transformed follicle after ovulation that secretes progesterone

corpus spongiosum.meaning: column of erectile tissue in the penis that fills with blood during an erection and surrounds the penile urethra on the ventral portion of the penis

cortex.meaning: in hair, the second or middle layer of keratinocytes originating from the hair matrix, as seen in a cross-section of the hair bulb

cortical nephrons.meaning: nephrons with loops of Henle that do not extend into the renal medulla
