corticobulbar tract.meaning: connection between the cortex and the brainstem responsible for generating movement

corticospinal tract.meaning: connection between the cortex and the spinal cord responsible for generating movement

cortisol.meaning: glucocorticoid important in gluconeogenesis, the catabolism of glycogen, and downregulation of the immune system

costal cartilage.meaning: hyaline cartilage structure attached to the anterior end of each rib that provides for either direct or indirect attachment of most ribs to the sternum

costal facet.meaning: site on the lateral sides of a thoracic vertebra for articulation with the head of a rib

costal groove.meaning: shallow groove along the inferior margin of a rib that provides passage for blood vessels and a nerve

costoclavicular ligament.meaning: band of connective tissue that unites the medial clavicle with the first rib

countercurrent multiplier system.meaning: involves the descending and ascending loops of Henle directing forming urine in opposing directions to create a concentration gradient when combined with variable permeability and sodium pumping

covalent bond.meaning: chemical bond in which two atoms share electrons, thereby completing their valence shells

cranial.meaning: describes a position above or higher than another part of the body proper; also referred to as superior

cranial cavity.meaning: division of the posterior (dorsal) cavity that houses the brain

cranial nerve.meaning: one of twelve nerves connected to the brain that are responsible for sensory or motor functions of the head and neck

cranial nerve exam.meaning: major section of the neurological exam that assesses sensory and motor functions of the cranial nerves and their associated central and peripheral structures

craniosacral system.meaning: alternate name for the parasympathetic division of the autonomic nervous system that is based on the anatomical location of central neurons in brainstem nuclei and the lateral horn of the sacral spinal cord; also referred to as craniosacral outflow

creatine phosphate.meaning: phosphagen used to store energy from ATP and transfer it to muscle

cribriform plate.meaning: small, flattened areas with numerous small openings, located to either side of the midline in the floor of the anterior cranial fossa; formed by the ethmoid bone

cricoid cartilage.meaning: portion of the larynx composed of a ring of cartilage with a wide posterior region and a thinner anterior region; attached to the oesophagus

crista galli.meaning: small upward projection located at the midline in the floor of the anterior cranial fossa; formed by the ethmoid bone

cross matching.meaning: blood test for identification of blood type using antibodies and small samples of blood

crown.meaning: portion of tooth visible superior to the gum line

cuboid.meaning: tarsal bone that articulates posteriorly with the calcaneus bone, medially with the lateral cuneiform bone, and anteriorly with the fourth and fifth metatarsal bones

cupula.meaning: specialised structure within the base of a semicircular canal that bends the stereocilia of hair cells when the head rotates by way of the relative movement of the enclosed fluid

cuspid.meaning: (also, canine) pointed tooth used for tearing and shredding food

cutaneous membrane.meaning: skin; epithelial tissue made up of a stratified squamous epithelial cells that cover the outside of the body

cuticle.meaning: in hair, the outermost layer of keratinocytes originating from the hair matrix, as seen in a cross-section of the hair bulb

cyclic adenosine monophosphate.meaning: second messenger that, in response to adenylyl cyclase activation, triggers a phosphorylation cascade

cyclin.meaning: one of a group of proteins that function in the progression of the cell cycle

cyclin-dependent kinase.meaning: one of a group of enzymes associated with cyclins that help them perform their functions

cystic artery.meaning: branch of the common hepatic artery; supplies blood to the gall bladder

cystic duct.meaning: duct through which bile drains and enters the gallbladder

cytoarchitecture.meaning: study of a tissue based on the structure and organisation of its cellular components; related to the broader term, histology

cytokines.meaning: class of proteins that act as autocrine or paracrine signalling molecules; in the cardiovascular system, they stimulate the proliferation of progenitor cells and help to stimulate both nonspecific and specific resistance to disease

cytokinesis.meaning: final stage in cell division, where the cytoplasm divides to form two separate daughter cells

cytoplasm.meaning: internal material between the cell membrane and nucleus of a cell, mainly consisting of a water-based fluid called cytosol, within which are all the other organelles and cellular solute and suspended materials

cytoskeleton.meaning: “skeleton” of a cell; formed by rod-like proteins that support the cell’s shape and provide, among other functions, locomotive abilities

cytosol.meaning: clear, semi-fluid medium of the cytoplasm, made up mostly of water

cytotoxic t cells.meaning: T lymphocytes with the ability to induce apoptosis in target cells

dalton’s law.meaning: statement of the principle that a specific gas type in a mixture exerts its own pressure, as if that specific gas type was not part of a mixture of gases

decussate.meaning: to cross the midline, as in fibres that project from one side of the body to the other

deep.meaning: describes a position farther from the surface of the body

deep femoral vein.meaning: drains blood from the deeper portions of the thigh and leads to the femoral vein

deep posterior compartment of the forear.term: deep posterior compartment of the forearm

deep tendon reflex.meaning: another term for stretch reflex, based on the elicitation through deep stimulation of the tendon at the insertion

defecation.meaning: elimination of undigested substances from the body in the form of faeces

defensins.meaning: antimicrobial proteins released from neutrophils and macrophages that create openings in the plasma membranes to kill cells

dehydration.meaning: state of containing insufficient water in blood and other tissues

delta cell.meaning: minor cell type in the pancreas that secretes the hormone somatostatin

deltoid.meaning: shoulder muscle that abducts the arm as well as flexes and medially rotates it, and extends and laterally rotates it

denaturation.meaning: change in the structure of a molecule through physical or chemical means

dendrite.meaning: one of many branchlike processes that extends from the neuron cell body and functions as a contact for incoming signals (synapses) from other neurons or sensory cells

dens.meaning: bony projection (odontoid process) that extends upward from the body of the C2 (axis) vertebra

dense body.meaning: sarcoplasmic structure that attaches to the sarcolemma and shortens the muscle as thin filaments slide past thick filaments

dentine.meaning: bone-like tissue immediately deep to the enamel of the crown or cementum of the root of a tooth

deoxyribonucleic acid.meaning: deoxyribose-containing nucleotide that stores genetic information

depolarisation.meaning: change in a cell membrane potential from rest toward zero

depression.meaning: downward (inferior) motion of the scapula or mandible

dermal papilla.meaning: (plural = dermal papillae) extension of the papillary layer of the dermis that increases surface contact between the epidermis and dermis

dermis.meaning: layer of skin between the epidermis and hypodermis, composed mainly of connective tissue and containing blood vessels, hair follicles, sweat glands, and other structures

descending aorta.meaning: portion of the aorta that continues downward past the end of the aortic arch; subdivided into the thoracic aorta and the abdominal aorta

descending colon.meaning: part of the colon between the transverse colon and the sigmoid colon

descending tract.meaning: central nervous system fibres carrying motor commands from the brain to the spinal cord or periphery

desmosome.meaning: structure that forms an impermeable junction between cells

development.meaning: changes an organism goes through during its life

diacylglycerol.meaning: molecule that, like cAMP, activates protein kinases, thereby initiating a phosphorylation cascade

diaphragm.meaning: skeletal muscle that separates the thoracic and abdominal cavities and is dome-shaped at rest

diaphysis.meaning: tubular shaft that runs between the proximal and distal ends of a long bone

diastole.meaning: period of time when the heart muscle is relaxed and the chambers fill with blood

diencephalon.meaning: region of the adult brain that retains its name from embryonic development and includes the thalamus and hypothalamus

differentiation.meaning: process by which unspecialised cells become specialised in structure and function

diffusion.meaning: movement of a substance from an area of higher concentration to one of lower concentration

digastric.meaning: muscle that has anterior and posterior bellies and elevates the hyoid bone and larynx when one swallows; it also depresses the mandible

digital arteries.meaning: formed from the superficial and deep palmar arches; supply blood to the digits

dihydroxyvitamin d.meaning: active form of vitamin D required by the intestinal epithelial cells for the absorption of calcium

dilation.meaning: first stage of childbirth, involving an increase in cervical diameter

dipeptidase.meaning: brush border enzyme that acts on proteins

diploë.meaning: layer of spongy bone, that is sandwiched between the two layers of compact bone found in flat bones

distal.meaning: describes a position farther from the point of attachment or the trunk of the body

dorsal.meaning: describes the back or direction toward the back of the body; also referred to as posterior

dorsal column system.meaning: ascending tract of the spinal cord associated with fine touch and proprioceptive sensations

dorsal group.meaning: region that includes the extensor digitorum brevis

dorsal nucleus of the vagus nerve.term: dorsal nucleus of the vagus nerve

dorsum nasi.meaning: intermediate portion of the external nose that connects the bridge to the apex and is supported by the nasal bone

downregulation.meaning: decrease in the number of hormone receptors, typically in response to chronically excessive levels of a hormone

ductus arteriosus.meaning: shunt in the pulmonary trunk that diverts oxygenated blood back to the aorta

ductus deferens.meaning: (also, vas deferens) duct that transports sperm from the epididymis through the spermatic cord and into the ejaculatory duct; also referred as the vas deferens

duodenal gland.meaning: (also, Brunner’s gland) mucous-secreting gland in the duodenal submucosa

duodenum.meaning: first part of the small intestine, which starts at the pyloric sphincter and ends at the jejunum

ear ossicles.meaning: three small bones located in the middle ear cavity that serve to transmit sound vibrations to the inner ear

early induced immune response.meaning: includes antimicrobial proteins stimulated during the first several days of an infection

eccentric contraction.meaning: muscle contraction that lengthens the muscle as the tension is diminished

eccrine sweat gland.meaning: type of sweat gland that is common throughout the skin surface; it produces a hypotonic sweat for thermoregulation

ectoderm.meaning: outermost embryonic germ layer from which the epidermis and the nervous tissue derive

ectopic pregnancy.meaning: implantation of an embryo outside of the uterus

eczema.meaning: skin condition due to an allergic reaction, which resembles a rash

edinger–westphal nucleus.meaning: location of parasympathetic neurons that project to the ciliary ganglion

effector.meaning: organ that can cause a change in a value

effector t cells.meaning: immune cells with a direct, adverse effect on a pathogen

efferent arteriole.meaning: arteriole carrying blood from the glomerulus to the capillary beds around the convoluted tubules and loop of Henle; portion of the portal system

ejaculatory duct.meaning: duct that connects the ampulla of the ductus deferens with the duct of the seminal vesicle at the prostatic urethra

ejection fraction.meaning: portion of the blood that is pumped or ejected from the heart with each contraction; mathematically represented by SV divided by EDV

elastic cartilage.meaning: type of cartilage, with elastin as the major protein, characterised by rigid support as well as elasticity

elastic fibre.meaning: fibrous protein within connective tissue that contains a high percentage of the protein elastin that allows the fibres to stretch and return to original size

elastin fibres.meaning: fibres made of the protein elastin that increase the elasticity of the dermis

elbow joint.meaning: joint located between the upper arm and forearm regions of the upper limb; formed by the articulations between the trochlea of the humerus and the trochlear notch of the ulna, and the capitulum of the humerus and the head of the radius

electrical gradient.meaning: difference in the electrical charge (potential) between two regions

electrical synapse.meaning: connection between two neurons, or any two electrically active cells, where ions flow directly through channels spanning their adjacent cell membranes

electrocardiogram.meaning: surface recording of the electrical activity of the heart that can be used for diagnosis of irregular heart function; also abbreviated as EKG

electrochemical exclusion.meaning: principle of selectively allowing ions through a channel on the basis of their charge

electron.meaning: subatomic particle having a negative charge and nearly no mass; found orbiting the atom’s nucleus

element.meaning: substance that cannot be created or broken down by ordinary chemical means

elevation.meaning: upward (superior) motion of the scapula or mandible

emigration.meaning: (also, diapedesis) process by which leukocytes squeeze through adjacent cells in a blood vessel wall to enter tissues

enamel.meaning: covering of the dentine of the crown of a tooth

end diastolic volume.meaning: (also, preload) the amount of blood in the ventricles at the end of atrial systole just prior to ventricular contraction

end systolic volume.meaning: amount of blood remaining in each ventricle following systole

endocardial tubes.meaning: stage in which lumens form within the expanding cardiogenic cords, forming hollow structures

endochondral ossification.meaning: process in which bone forms by replacing hyaline cartilage

endocrine system.meaning: cells, tissues, and organs that secrete hormones as a primary or secondary function and play an integral role in normal bodily processes

endocytosis.meaning: import of material into the cell by formation of a membrane-bound vesicle

endoderm.meaning: innermost embryonic germ layer from which most of the digestive system and lower respiratory system derive

endogenous.meaning: describes substance made in the human body

endogenous chemical.meaning: substance produced and released within the body to interact with a receptor protein

endometrium.meaning: inner lining of the uterus, part of which builds up during the secretory phase of the menstrual cycle and then sheds with menses

endomysium.meaning: loose, and well-hydrated connective tissue covering each muscle fibre in a skeletal muscle

endoneurium.meaning: innermost layer of connective tissue that surrounds individual axons within a nerve

endosteum.meaning: delicate membranous lining of a bone’s medullary cavity

enteroendocrine cell.meaning: gastric gland cell that releases hormones

enterokinase.meaning: enzyme located in the wall of the small intestine that activates trypsin

enteropeptidase.meaning: intestinal brush-border enzyme that activates trypsinogen to trypsin

enzyme.meaning: protein or RNA that catalyses chemical reactions

eosinophils.meaning: granulocytes that stain with eosin; they release antihistamines and are especially active against parasitic worms

ependymal cell.meaning: glial cell type in the CNS responsible for producing cerebrospinal fluid

epiblast.meaning: upper layer of cells of the embryonic disc that forms from the inner cell mass; gives rise to all three germ layers

epicardial coronary arteries.meaning: surface arteries of the heart that generally follow the sulci

epicranial aponeurosis.meaning: (also, galea aponeurosis) flat broad tendon that connects the frontalis and occipitalis

epidermis.meaning: outermost tissue layer of the skin

epididymis.meaning: (plural = epididymides) coiled tubular structure in which sperm start to mature and are stored until ejaculation

epiglottis.meaning: leaf-shaped piece of elastic cartilage that is a portion of the larynx that swings to close the trachea during swallowing

epimysium.meaning: outer layer of connective tissue around a skeletal muscle

epinephrine.meaning: signalling molecule released from the adrenal medulla into the bloodstream as part of the sympathetic response

epineurium.meaning: outermost layer of connective tissue that surrounds an entire nerve

epiphyseal line.meaning: completely ossified remnant of the epiphyseal plate

epiphyseal plate.meaning: (also, growth plate) sheet of hyaline cartilage in the metaphysis of an immature bone; replaced by bone tissue as the organ grows in length

epiphysis.meaning: wide section at each end of a long bone; filled with spongy bone and red marrow

epiploic appendage.meaning: small sac of fat-filled visceral peritoneum attached to teniae coli

epithalamus.meaning: region of the diencephalon containing the pineal gland

epithelial membrane.meaning: epithelium attached to a layer of connective tissue

esophageal artery.meaning: branch of the thoracic aorta; supplies blood to the oesophagus

excitation-contraction coupling.meaning: sequence of events from motor neuron signalling to a skeletal muscle fibre to contraction of the fibre’s sarcomeres

executive functions.meaning: cognitive processes of the prefrontal cortex that lead to directing goal-directed behaviour, which is a precursor to executing motor commands

exocrine gland.meaning: group of epithelial cells that secrete substances through ducts that open to the skin or to internal body surfaces that lead to the exterior of the body

exocrine system.meaning: cells, tissues, and organs that secrete substances directly to target tissues via glandular ducts

exocytosis.meaning: export of a substance out of a cell by formation of a membrane-bound vesicle

exogenous.meaning: describes substance made outside of the human body

exon.meaning: one of the coding regions of an mRNA molecule that remain after splicing

expulsion.meaning: second stage of childbirth, during which the mother bears down with contractions; this stage ends in birth

hormone receptor.meaning: protein within a cell or on the cell membrane that binds a hormone, initiating the target cell response

humeroradial joint.meaning: articulation between the capitulum of the humerus and head of the radius

humeroulnar joint.meaning: articulation between the trochlea of humerus and the trochlear notch of the ulna; uniaxial hinge joint that allows for flexion/extension of the forearm

humerus.meaning: single bone of the upper arm

hyaline cartilage.meaning: most common type of cartilage, smooth and made of short collagen fibres embedded in a chondroitin sulfate ground substance

hydrochloric acid.meaning: digestive acid secreted by parietal cells in the stomach

hydrogen bond.meaning: dipole-dipole bond in which a hydrogen atom covalently bonded to an electronegative atom is weakly attracted to a second electronegative atom

hydrophilic.meaning: describes a substance or structure attracted to water

hydrophobic.meaning: describes a substance or structure repelled by water

hydrostatic pressure.meaning: pressure exerted by a fluid against a wall, caused by its own weight or pumping force

hydroxymethylglutaryl coa (hmg coa).meaning: molecule created in the first step of the creation of ketone bodies from acetyl CoA

hymen.meaning: membrane that covers part of the opening of the vagina

hyoglossus.meaning: muscle that originates on the hyoid bone to move the tongue downward and flatten it

hyoid bone.meaning: small, U-shaped bone located in upper neck that does not contact any other bone

hypercapnia.meaning: abnormally elevated blood levels of CO2

hyperextension.meaning: excessive extension of joint, beyond the normal range of movement

hyperflexion.meaning: excessive flexion of joint, beyond the normal range of movement

hypernatraemia.meaning: abnormal increase in blood sodium levels

hyperparathyroidism.meaning: disorder caused by overproduction of PTH that results in abnormally elevated blood calcium

hyperplasia.meaning: process in which one cell splits to produce new cells

hyperpnea.meaning: increased rate and depth of ventilation due to an increase in oxygen demand that does not significantly alter blood oxygen or carbon dioxide levels

hypertension.meaning: chronic and persistent blood pressure measurements of 140/90 mm Hg or above

hypertonic.meaning: describes a solution concentration that is higher than a reference concentration

hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.meaning: pathological enlargement of the heart, generally for no known reason

hypertrophy.meaning: addition of structural proteins to muscle fibres

hyperventilation.meaning: increased ventilation rate that leads to abnormally low blood carbon dioxide levels and high (alkaline) blood pH

hypervolaemia.meaning: abnormally high levels of fluid and blood within the body

hypoblast.meaning: lower layer of cells of the embryonic disc that extend into the blastocoel to form the yolk sac

hypocapnia.meaning: abnormally low blood levels of CO2

hypodermis.meaning: connective tissue connecting the integument to the underlying bone and muscle

hypokalaemia.meaning: abnormally decreased blood levels of potassium

hyponatraemia.meaning: lower-than-normal levels of sodium in the blood

hyponychium.meaning: thickened layer of stratum corneum that lies below the free edge of the nail

hypoparathyroidism.meaning: disorder caused by underproduction of PTH that results in abnormally low blood calcium

hypothalamus.meaning: major region of the diencephalon that is responsible for coordinating autonomic and endocrine control of homeostasis

hypothenar.meaning: group of muscles on the medial aspect of the palm

hypotonia.meaning: abnormally low muscle tone caused by the absence of low-level contractions

hypotonic.meaning: describes a solution concentration that is lower than a reference concentration

hypotonicity.meaning: low muscle tone, a sign of LMN disease

hypovolaemic shock.meaning: type of circulatory shock caused by excessive loss of blood volume due to haemorrhage or possibly dehydration

hypoxaemia.meaning: below-normal level of oxygen saturation of blood (typically <95 percent)

igd.meaning: class of antibody whose only known function is as a receptor on naive B cells; important in B cell activation

ige.meaning: antibody that binds to mast cells and causes antigen-specific degranulation during an allergic response

igg.meaning: main blood antibody of late primary and early secondary responses; passed from carrier to unborn child via placenta

igm.meaning: antibody whose monomer is a surface receptor of naive B cells; the pentamer is the first antibody made blood plasma during primary responses

ileocecal sphincter.meaning: sphincter located where the small intestine joins with the large intestine

ileum.meaning: end of the small intestine between the jejunum and the large intestine

iliac crest.meaning: curved, superior margin of the ilium

iliac fossa.meaning: shallow depression found on the anterior and medial surfaces of the upper ilium

iliacus.meaning: muscle that, along with the psoas major, makes up the iliopsoas

iliococcygeus.meaning: muscle that makes up the levator ani along with the pubococcygeus

iliocostalis cervicis.meaning: muscle of the iliocostalis group associated with the cervical region

iliocostalis group.meaning: laterally placed muscles of the erector spinae

iliocostalis lumborum.meaning: muscle of the iliocostalis group associated with the lumbar region

iliocostalis thoracis.meaning: muscle of the iliocostalis group associated with the thoracic region

iliofemoral ligament.meaning: intrinsic ligament spanning from the ilium of the hip bone to the femur, on the superior-anterior aspect of the hip joint

iliopsoas group.meaning: muscle group consisting of iliacus and psoas major muscles, that flexes the thigh at the hip, rotates it laterally, and flexes the trunk of the body onto the hip

ilium.meaning: superior portion of the hip bone

immediate hypersensitivity.meaning: (type I) IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation caused by crosslinking of surface IgE by antigen

immune system.meaning: series of barriers, cells, and soluble mediators that combine to response to infections of the body with pathogenic organisms

immunoglobulin.meaning: protein antibody; occurs as one of five main classes

implantation.meaning: process by which a blastocyst embeds itself in the uterine endometrium

inactivation gate.meaning: part of a voltage-gated Na+ channel that closes when the membrane potential reaches +30 mV

inactive proenzymes.meaning: forms in which proteases are stored and released to prevent the inappropriate digestion of the native proteins of the stomach, pancreas, and small intestine

incisor.meaning: midline, chisel-shaped tooth used for cutting into food

incomplete dominance.meaning: pattern of inheritance in which a heterozygous genotype expresses a phenotype intermediate between dominant and recessive phenotypes

incontinence.meaning: loss of ability to control micturition

incus.meaning: (also, anvil) ossicle of the middle ear that connects the malleus to the stapes

indirect pathway.meaning: connections within the basal nuclei from the striatum through the globus pallidus external segment and subthalamic nucleus to the globus pallidus internal segment/substantia nigra pars compacta that result in inhibition of the thalamus to decrease cortical control of movement

inferior articular process.meaning: bony process that extends downward from the vertebral arch of a vertebra that articulates with the superior articular process of the next lower vertebra

inferior colliculus.meaning: half of the midbrain tectum that is part of the brainstem auditory pathway

inferior mesenteric ganglion.meaning: one of the collateral ganglia of the sympathetic system that projects to the digestive system

inferior olive.meaning: nucleus in the medulla that is involved in processing information related to motor control

inferior phrenic artery.meaning: branch of the abdominal aorta; supplies blood to the inferior surface of the diaphragm

inferior pubic ramus.meaning: narrow segment of bone that passes inferiorly and laterally from the pubic body; joins with the ischial ramus to form the ischiopubic ramus

infraglenoid tubercle.meaning: small bump or roughened area located on the lateral border of the scapula, near the inferior margin of the glenoid cavity

infraspinatus.meaning: muscle that laterally rotates the arm

infraspinous fossa.meaning: broad depression located on the posterior scapula, inferior to the spine

infundibulum.meaning: (of the uterine tube) wide, distal portion of the uterine tube terminating in fimbriae

inguinal canal.meaning: opening in abdominal wall that connects the testes to the abdominal cavity

inhibin.meaning: hormone secreted by the male and female gonads that inhibits FSH production by the anterior pituitary

initial segment.meaning: first part of the axon as it emerges from the axon hillock, where the electrical signals known as action potentials are generated

innate immune response.meaning: rapid but relatively nonspecific immune response

inner cell mass.meaning: cluster of cells within the blastocyst that is fated to become the embryo

inner ear.meaning: structure within the temporal bone that contains the sensory apparati of hearing and balance

inner segment.meaning: in the eye, the section of a photoreceptor that contains the nucleus and other major organelles for normal cellular functions

inner synaptic layer.meaning: layer in the retina where bipolar cells connect to RGCs

innermost intercostal.meaning: the deepest intercostal muscles that draw the ribs together

inorganic compound.meaning: substance that does not contain both carbon and hydrogen

inositol triphosphate (ip3).meaning: molecule that initiates the release of calcium ions from intracellular stores

insertion.meaning: end of a skeletal muscle that is attached to the structure (usually a bone) that is moved when the muscle contracts

inspiration.meaning: (also, inhalation) process that causes air to enter the lungs

inspiratory capacity.meaning: sum of the TV and IRV, which is the amount of air that can maximally be inhaled past a tidal expiration

insulin.meaning: hormone secreted by the pancreas that stimulates the uptake of glucose into the cells

insulin-like growth factors.meaning: protein that enhances cellular proliferation, inhibits apoptosis, and stimulates the cellular uptake of amino acids for protein synthesis

integral protein.meaning: membrane-associated protein that spans the entire width of the lipid bilayer

integration.meaning: nervous system function that combines sensory perceptions and higher cognitive functions (memories, learning, emotion, etc.) to produce a response

intercalated cell.meaning: specialised cell of the collecting ducts that secrete or absorb acid or bicarbonate; important in acid–base balance

intercalated disc.meaning: part of the sarcolemma that connects cardiac tissue, and contains gap junctions and desmosomes

intercondylar eminence.meaning: irregular elevation on the superior end of the tibia, between the articulating surfaces of the medial and lateral condyles

intercondylar fossa.meaning: deep depression on the posterior side of the distal femur that separates the medial and lateral condyles

intercostal artery.meaning: branch of the thoracic aorta; supplies blood to the muscles of the thoracic cavity and vertebral column

intercostal muscles.meaning: muscles that span the spaces between the ribs

intercostal nerve.meaning: systemic nerve in the thoracic cavity that is found between two ribs

intercostal vein.meaning: drains the muscles of the thoracic wall and leads to the azygos vein

interferons.meaning: early induced proteins made in virally infected cells that cause nearby cells to make antiviral proteins

interleukins.meaning: signalling molecules that may function in haemopoiesis, inflammation, and specific immune responses

intermediate cuneiform.meaning: middle of the three cuneiform tarsal bones; articulates posteriorly with the navicular bone, medially with the medial cuneiform bone, laterally with the lateral cuneiform bone, and anteriorly with the second metatarsal bone

intermediate filament.meaning: type of cytoskeletal filament made of keratin, characterised by an intermediate thickness, and playing a role in resisting cellular tension

internal acoustic meatus.meaning: opening into petrous ridge, located on the lateral wall of the posterior cranial fossa

internal anal sphincter.meaning: involuntary smooth muscle sphincter in the anal canal

internal capsule.meaning: segment of the descending motor pathway that passes between the caudate nucleus and the putamen

internal elastic membrane.meaning: membrane composed of elastic fibres that separates the tunica intima from the tunica media; seen in larger arteries

internal intercostal.meaning: muscles the intermediate intercostal muscles that draw the ribs together

internal oblique.meaning: flat, intermediate abdominal muscle with fascicles that run perpendicular to those of the external oblique

internal respiration.meaning: gas exchange that occurs at the level of body tissues

internal root sheath.meaning: innermost layer of keratinocytes in the hair follicle that surround the hair root up to the hair shaft

internal thoracic vein.meaning: (also, internal mammary vein) drains the anterior surface of the chest wall and leads to the brachiocephalic vein

internal urinary sphincter.meaning: smooth muscle at the juncture of the bladder and urethra; relaxes as the bladder fills to allow urine into the urethra

internodal pathways.meaning: specialised conductile cells within the atria that transmit the impulse from the SA node throughout the myocardial cells of the atrium and to the AV node

interosseous membrane of the leg.meaning: sheet of dense connective tissue that unites the shafts of the tibia and fibula bones

interphase.meaning: entire life cycle of a cell, excluding mitosis

interstitial fluid hydrostatic pressure.meaning: force exerted by the fluid in the tissue spaces

intestinal phase.meaning: phase of gastric secretion that begins when chyme enters the intestine

intorsion.meaning: medial rotation of the eye around its axis

intra-alveolar pressure.meaning: (intrapulmonary pressure) pressure of the air within the alveoli

intracellular fluid.meaning: fluid in the cytosol of cells

intramural ganglia.meaning: terminal ganglia of the parasympathetic system that are found within the walls of the target effector

intrapleural pressure.meaning: pressure of the air within the pleural cavity

intrinsic muscles of the hand.meaning: muscles that move the wrists, hands, and fingers and originate in the palm

intrinsic muscles of the tongue.meaning: muscles that originate out of, and insert into, other tissues within the tongue and control the shape of the tongue

intrinsic pathway.meaning: initial coagulation pathway that begins with vascular damage or contact with foreign substances, and results in the activation of the common pathway

intron.meaning: non-coding regions of a pre-mRNA transcript that may be removed during splicing

inulin.meaning: plant polysaccharide injected to determine GFR; is neither secreted nor absorbed by the kidney, so its appearance in the urine is directly proportional to its filtration rate

inversion.meaning: foot movement involving the intertarsal joints of the foot in which the bottom of the foot is turned toward the midline

ion.meaning: atom with an overall positive or negative charge

ionic bond.meaning: attraction between an anion and a cation

ionotropic receptor.meaning: neurotransmitter receptor that acts as an ion channel gate, and opens by the binding of the neurotransmitter

ipsilateral.meaning: word meaning on the same side, as in axons that do not cross the midline in a fibre tract

iris.meaning: coloured portion of the anterior eye that surrounds the pupil

irregular bone.meaning: bone of complex shape; protects internal organs from compressive forces

ischaemia.meaning: insufficient blood flow to the tissues

ischial spine.meaning: pointed, bony projection from the posterior margin of the ischium that separates the greater sciatic notch and lesser sciatic notch

ischiococcygeus.meaning: muscle that assists the levator ani and pulls the coccyx anteriorly

ischiofemoral ligament.meaning: intrinsic ligament spanning from the ischium of the hip bone to the femur, on the posterior aspect of the hip joint

ischiopubic ramus.meaning: narrow extension of bone that connects the ischial tuberosity to the pubic body; formed by the junction of the ischial ramus and inferior pubic ramus

ischium.meaning: posteroinferior portion of the hip bone

isotonic.meaning: describes a solution concentration that is the same as a reference concentration

isotonic contraction.meaning: muscle contraction that involves changes in muscle length

isotope.meaning: one of the variations of an element in which the number of neutrons differ from each other

isthmus.meaning: narrow, medial portion of the uterine tube that joins the uterus

jaw-jerk reflex.meaning: stretch reflex of the masseter muscle

jejunum.meaning: middle part of the small intestine between the duodenum and the ileum

joint.meaning: site at which two or more bones or bone and cartilage come together (articulate)

karyotype.meaning: systematic arrangement of images of chromosomes into homologous pairs

kinetochore.meaning: region of a centromere where microtubules attach to a pair of sister chromatids

korotkoff sounds.meaning: noises created by turbulent blood flow through the vessels

krebs cycle.meaning: also called the citric acid cycle or the tricarboxylic acid cycle, converts pyruvate into CO2 and high-energy FADH2, NADH, and ATP molecules

kyphosis.meaning: (also, humpback or hunchback) excessive posterior curvature of the thoracic vertebral column region

labia majora.meaning: hair-covered folds of skin located behind the mons pubis

labia minora.meaning: thin, pigmented, hairless flaps of skin located medial and deep to the labia majora

labial frenulum.meaning: midline mucous membrane fold that attaches the inner surface of the lips to the gums

lacrimal bone.meaning: paired bones that contribute to the anterior-medial wall of each orbit

lanugo.meaning: silk-like hairs that coat the fetus; shed later in fetal development

laryngopharynx.meaning: part of the pharynx that functions in respiration and digestion

laryngotracheal.meaning: bud forms from the lung bud, has a tracheal end and bulbous bronchial buds at the distal end

larynx.meaning: cartilaginous structure that produces the voice, prevents food and beverages from entering the trachea, and regulates the volume of air that enters and leaves the lungs

latent period.meaning: the time when a twitch does not produce contraction

lateral.meaning: describes the side or direction toward the side of the body

lateral apertures.meaning: pair of openings from the fourth ventricle to the subarachnoid space on either side and between the medulla and cerebellum

lateral epicondyle of the humerus.meaning: small projection located on the lateral side of the distal humerus

lateral excursion.meaning: side-to-side movement of the mandible away from the midline, toward either the right or left side

light chain.meaning: small protein chain of an antibody

polycythaemia.meaning: elevated level of haemoglobin, whether adaptive or pathological

polymorphonuclear.meaning: having a lobed nucleus, as seen in some leukocytes

polypeptide.meaning: chain of amino acids linked by peptide bonds

polyribosome.meaning: simultaneous translation of a single mRNA transcript by multiple ribosomes

polysaccharide.meaning: compound consisting of more than two carbohydrate monomers bonded by dehydration synthesis via glycosidic bonds

polysaccharides.meaning: complex carbohydrates made up of many monosaccharides

polyspermy.meaning: penetration of an oocyte by more than one sperm

polyuria.meaning: urine production in excess of 2.5 L/day; may be caused by diabetes insipidus, diabetes mellitus, or excessive use of diuretics

popliteal artery.meaning: continuation of the femoral artery posterior to the knee; branches into the anterior and posterior tibial arteries

popliteal fossa.meaning: diamond-shaped space at the back of the knee

popliteal vein.meaning: continuation of the femoral vein behind the knee; drains the region behind the knee and forms from the fusion of the fibular and anterior and posterior tibial veins

popliteus.meaning: muscle that flexes the leg at the knee and creates the floor of the popliteal fossa

porta hepatis.meaning: “gateway to the liver” where the hepatic artery and hepatic portal vein enter the liver

portal triad.meaning: bile duct, hepatic artery branch, and hepatic portal vein branch

positive chemotaxis.meaning: process in which a cell is attracted to move in the direction of chemical stimuli

positive feedback.meaning: mechanism that intensifies a change in the body’s physiological condition in response to a stimulus

positive inotropic factors.meaning: factors that positively impact or increase heart contractility

positive selection.meaning: selection of thymocytes within the thymus that interact with self, but not non-self, MHC molecules

positron emission tomography.meaning: medical imaging technique in which radiopharmaceuticals are traced to reveal metabolic and physiological functions in tissues

postabsorptive state.meaning: also called the fasting state; the metabolic state occurring after digestion when food is no longer the body’s source of energy and it must rely on stored glycogen

postcentral gyrus.meaning: ridge just posterior to the central sulcus, in the parietal lobe, where somatosensory processing initially takes place in the cerebrum

posterior.meaning: describes the back or direction toward the back of the body; also referred to as dorsal

posterior arch.meaning: posterior portion of the ring-like C1 (atlas) vertebra

posterior cranial fossa.meaning: deepest and most posterior cranial fossa; extends from the petrous ridge to the occipital bone

posterior inferior iliac spine.meaning: small, bony projection located at the inferior margin of the auricular surface on the posterior ilium

posterior longitudinal ligament.meaning: ligament that runs the length of the vertebral column, uniting the posterior sides of the vertebral bodies

posterior median sulcus.meaning: midline feature of the posterior spinal cord, marking the separation between right and left sides of the cord

posterior scalene.meaning: smallest scalene muscle, located posterior to the middle scalene

posterior superior iliac spine.meaning: rounded, posterior end of the iliac crest

potential energy.meaning: stored energy matter possesses because of the positioning or structure of its components

power stroke.meaning: action of myosin pulling actin inward (toward the M line)

pp cell.meaning: minor cell type in the pancreas that secretes the hormone pancreatic polypeptide

praxis.meaning: in a neurological exam, the act of doing something using ready knowledge or skills in response to verbal instruction

precapillary sphincters.meaning: circular rings of smooth muscle that surround the entrance to a capillary and regulate blood flow into that capillary

precentral gyrus.meaning: ridge just anterior to the central sulcus, in the frontal lobe, the primary motor cortex is located

precentral gyrus of the frontal cortex.term: precentral gyrus of the frontal cortex

prefrontal lobe.meaning: specific region of the frontal lobe anterior to the more specific motor function areas, which can be related to the early planning of movements and intentions to the point of being personality-type functions

preganglionic fibre.meaning: axon from a central neuron in the autonomic nervous system that projects to and synapses with a ganglionic neuron; sometimes referred to as a preganglionic neuron

preload.meaning: (also, end diastolic volume) amount of blood in the ventricles at the end of atrial systole just prior to ventricular contraction

premolar.meaning: (also, bicuspid) transitional tooth used for mastication, crushing, and grinding food

premotor area.meaning: region of the frontal lobe responsible for planning movements that will be executed through the primary motor cortex

premotor cortex.meaning: cortical area anterior to the primary motor cortex that is responsible for planning movements

pressure.meaning: force exerted by a substance in contact with another substance

prevertebral ganglia.meaning: autonomic ganglia that are anterior to the vertebral column and functionally related to the sympathetic chain ganglia

primary adaptive response.meaning: immune system’s response to the first exposure to a pathogen

primary curve.meaning: anteriorly concave curvatures of the thoracic and sacrococcygeal regions that are retained from the original fetal curvature of the vertebral column

primary follicles.meaning: ovarian follicles with a primary oocyte and one layer of cuboidal granulosa cells

primary ossification centre.meaning: region, deep in the periosteal collar, where bone development starts during endochondral ossification

prime mover.meaning: (also, agonist) principle muscle involved in an action

primitive ventricle.meaning: portion of the primitive heart tube that eventually forms the left ventricle

primordial follicles.meaning: least developed ovarian follicles that consist of a single oocyte and a single layer of flat (squamous) granulosa cells

principal cell.meaning: found in collecting ducts and possess channels for the recovery or loss of sodium and potassium; under the control of aldosterone; also have aquaporin channels under ADH control to regulate recovery of water

process.meaning: in cells, an extension of a cell body; in the case of neurons, this includes the axon and dendrites

product.meaning: one or more substances produced by a chemical reaction

projection.meaning: bone markings where part of the surface sticks out above the rest of the surface, where tendons and ligaments attach

promoter.meaning: region of DNA that signals transcription to begin at that site within the gene

pubis.meaning: anterior portion of the hip bone

pubococcygeus.meaning: muscle that makes up the levator ani along with the iliococcygeus

pulmonary arteries.meaning: left and right branches of the pulmonary trunk that carry deoxygenated blood from the heart to each of the lungs

pulmonary trunk.meaning: single large vessel exiting the right ventricle that divides to form the right and left pulmonary arteries

pulse.meaning: alternating expansion and recoil of an artery as blood moves through the vessel; an indicator of heart rate

quiet breathing.meaning: (also, eupnea) mode of breathing that occurs at rest and does not require the cognitive thought of the individual

recessive.meaning: describes a trait that is only expressed in homozygous form and is masked in heterozygous form

recruitment.meaning: increase in the number of motor units involved in contraction

rectal valve.meaning: one of three transverse folds in the rectum where faeces is separated from flatus

rectum.meaning: part of the large intestine between the sigmoid colon and anal canal

rectus abdominis.meaning: long, linear muscle that extends along the middle of the trunk

rectus sheaths.meaning: tissue that makes up the linea alba

renal papillae.meaning: medullary area of the renal pyramids where collecting ducts empty urine into the minor calyces

renal pyramids.meaning: six to eight cone-shaped tissues in the medulla of the kidney containing collecting ducts and the loops of Henle of juxtamedullary nephrons

renal vein.meaning: largest vein entering the inferior vena cava; drains the kidneys and leads to the inferior vena cava

renewal.meaning: process by which worn-out cells are replaced

renin.meaning: enzyme produced by juxtaglomerular cells in response to decreased blood pressure or sympathetic nervous activity; catalyses the conversion of angiotensinogen into angiotensin I

repolarisation.meaning: return of the membrane potential to its normally negative voltage at the end of the action potential

reposition.meaning: movement of the thumb from opposition back to the anatomical position (next to index finger)

reproduction.meaning: process by which new organisms are generated

reserve zone.meaning: region of the epiphyseal plate that anchors the plate to the osseous tissue of the epiphysis

residual volume.meaning: amount of air that remains in the lungs after maximum exhalation

respiratory bronchiole.meaning: specific type of bronchiole that leads to alveolar sacs

respiratory cycle.meaning: one sequence of inspiration and expiration

respiratory epithelium.meaning: ciliated lining of much of the conducting zone that is specialised to remove debris and pathogens, and produce mucus

reticular lamina.meaning: matrix containing collagen and elastin secreted by connective tissue; a component of the basement membrane

reticulocyte.meaning: immature erythrocyte that may still contain fragments of organelles

retina.meaning: nervous tissue of the eye at which phototransduction takes place

retinacula.meaning: fibrous bands that sheath the tendons at the wrist

retinal.meaning: cofactor in an opsin molecule that undergoes a biochemical change when struck by a photon (pronounced with a stress on the last syllable)

retinal ganglion cell.meaning: neuron of the retina that projects along the second cranial nerve

retraction.meaning: posterior motion of the scapula or mandible

retrograde amnesia.meaning: loss of memories before a particular event

retroperitoneal.meaning: behind the peritoneum; in the case of the kidney and ureters, between the parietal peritoneum and the abdominal wall

rh blood group.meaning: blood-type classification based on the presence or absence of the antigen Rh on the erythrocyte membrane surface

rhodopsin.meaning: photopigment molecule found in the rod photoreceptors

rhombencephalon.meaning: primary vesicle of the embryonic brain that develops into the hindbrain, which includes the pons, cerebellum, and medulla

rhomboid major.meaning: muscle that attaches the vertebral border of the scapula to the spinous process of the thoracic vertebrae

rhomboid minor.meaning: muscle that attaches the vertebral border of the scapula to the spinous process of the thoracic vertebrae

ribosome.meaning: cellular organelle that functions in protein synthesis

ribs.meaning: thin, curved bones of the chest wall

root.meaning: portion of a tooth embedded in the alveolar processes beneath the gum line

s phase.meaning: stage of the cell cycle during which DNA replication occurs
