target effector.meaning: organ, tissue, or gland that will respond to the control of an autonomic or somatic or endocrine signal

target heart rate.meaning: range in which both the heart and lungs receive the maximum benefit from an aerobic workout

tarsal bone.meaning: one of the seven bones that make up the posterior foot; includes the calcaneus, talus, navicular, cuboid, medial cuneiform, intermediate cuneiform, and lateral cuneiform bones

taste buds.meaning: structures within a papilla on the tongue that contain gustatory receptor cells

tectorial membrane.meaning: component of the organ of Corti that lays over the hair cells, into which the stereocilia are embedded

tectospinal tract.meaning: extrapyramidal connections between the superior colliculus and spinal cord

tectum.meaning: region of the midbrain, thought of as the roof of the cerebral aqueduct, which is subdivided into the inferior and superior colliculi

tegmentum.meaning: region of the midbrain, thought of as the floor of the cerebral aqueduct, which continues into the pons and medulla as the floor of the fourth ventricle

telencephalon.meaning: secondary vesicle of the embryonic brain that develops into the cerebrum

telogen.meaning: resting phase of the hair growth cycle initiated with catagen and terminated by the beginning of a new anagen phase of hair growth

telophase.meaning: final stage of mitosis (and meiosis), preceding cytokinesis, characterised by the formation of two new daughter nuclei

temporal bone.meaning: paired bones that form the lateral, inferior portions of the skull, with squamous, mastoid, and petrous portions

temporal fossa.meaning: shallow space on the lateral side of the skull, above the level of the zygomatic arch

temporal lobe.meaning: region of the cerebral cortex directly beneath the temporal bone of the cranium

temporal process of the zygomatic bone.term: temporal process of the zygomatic bone
temporal process of the zygomatic bone.meaning: short extension from the zygomatic bone that forms the anterior portion of the zygomatic arch

temporal summation.meaning: combination of graded potentials at the same location on a neuron resulting in a strong signal from one input

temporal vein.meaning: drains blood from the temporal region and leads to the external jugular vein

temporomandibular joint.meaning: articulation between the condyle of the mandible and the mandibular fossa and articular tubercle of the temporal bone of the skull; allows for depression/elevation (opening/closing of mouth), protraction/retraction, and side-to-side motions of the mandible

tendinous intersections.meaning: three transverse bands of collagen fibres that divide the rectus abdominis into segments

tendon.meaning: dense connective tissue structure that anchors a muscle to bone

tendon sheath.meaning: connective tissue that surrounds a tendon at places where the tendon crosses a joint; contains a lubricating fluid to prevent friction and allow smooth movements of the tendon

tenia coli.meaning: one of three smooth muscle bands that make up the longitudinal muscle layer of the muscularis in all of the large intestine except the terminal end

tensor fascia lata.meaning: muscle that flexes and abducts the thigh

teres major.meaning: muscle that extends the arm and assists in adduction and medial rotation of it

teres minor.meaning: muscle that laterally rotates and extends the arm

terminal electron acceptor.meaning: oxygen, the recipient of the free hydrogen at the end of the electron transport chain

terminal ganglia.meaning: ganglia of the parasympathetic division of the autonomic system, which are located near or within the target effector, the latter also known as intramural ganglia

terminal ganglion.meaning: autonomic ganglia that are near or within the walls of organs that are responsible for contributing to homeostatic mechanisms of the autonomic nervous system

tertiary follicles.meaning: (also, antral follicles) ovarian follicles with a primary or secondary oocyte, multiple layers of granulosa cells, and a fully formed antrum

testicular artery.meaning: branch of the abdominal aorta; will ultimately travel outside the body cavity to the testes and form one component of the spermatic cord

testicular vein.meaning: drains the testes and forms part of the spermatic cord; the right testicular vein empties directly into the inferior vena cava and the left testicular vein empties into the left renal vein

testosterone.meaning: steroid hormone secreted by the testes and important in the maturation of sperm cells, growth and development of the reproductive system, and the development of secondary sex characteristics

th1 cells.meaning: cells that secrete cytokines that enhance the activity of macrophages and other cells

th2 cells.meaning: cells that secrete cytokines that induce B cells to differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells

thalamus.meaning: region of the central nervous system that acts as a relay for sensory pathways

thalassaemia.meaning: inherited blood disorder in which maturation of RBCs does not proceed normally, leading to abnormal formation of haemoglobin and the destruction of RBCs

theca cells.meaning: oestrogen-producing cells in a maturing ovarian follicle

thenar.meaning: group of muscles on the lateral aspect of the palm

thenar eminence.meaning: rounded contour of muscle at the base of the thumb

thermoneutral.meaning: external temperature at which the body does not expend any energy for thermoregulation, about 84 °F

thermoreceptor.meaning: type of sensory receptor capable of transducing temperature stimuli into neural action potentials

thermoregulation.meaning: process of regulating the temperature of the body

thick filament.meaning: the thick myosin strands and their multiple heads projecting from the centre of the sarcomere toward, but not all to way to, the Z-discs

thigh.meaning: portion of the lower limb located between the hip and knee joints

thin filament.meaning: thin strands of actin and its troponin-tropomyosin complex projecting from the Z-discs toward the centre of the sarcomere

third ventricle.meaning: portion of the ventricular system that is in the region of the diencephalon

third-degree burn.meaning: burn that penetrates and destroys the full thickness of the skin (epidermis and dermis)

thoracic aorta.meaning: portion of the descending aorta superior to the aortic hiatus

thoracic cage.meaning: consists of 12 pairs of ribs and sternum

thoracic cavity.meaning: division of the anterior (ventral) cavity that houses the heart, lungs, oesophagus, and trachea

thoracic curve.meaning: anteriorly concave curvature of the thoracic vertebral column region; a primary curve of the vertebral column

thoracic duct.meaning: large duct that drains lymph from the lower limbs, left thorax, left upper limb, and the left side of the head

thoracic vertebrae.meaning: twelve vertebrae numbered as T1–T12 that are located in the thoracic region (upper back) of the vertebral column

thoracic wall compliance.meaning: ability of the thoracic wall to stretch while under pressure

thoracolumbar system.meaning: alternate name for the sympathetic division of the autonomic nervous system that is based on the anatomical location of central neurons in the lateral horn of the thoracic and upper lumbar spinal cord

thoroughfare channel.meaning: continuation of the metarteriole that enables blood to bypass a capillary bed and flow directly into a venule, creating a vascular shunt

threshold.meaning: membrane voltage at which an action potential is initiated

thrombin.meaning: enzyme essential for the final steps in formation of a fibrin clot

thrombocytes.meaning: platelets, one of the formed elements of blood that consists of cell fragments broken off from megakaryocytes

thrombocytopenia.meaning: condition in which there are too few platelets, resulting in abnormal bleeding (haemophilia)

thrombocytosis.meaning: condition in which there are too many platelets, resulting in abnormal clotting (thrombosis)

thrombopoietin.meaning: hormone secreted by the liver and kidneys that prompts the development of megakaryocytes into thrombocytes (platelets)

thrombus.meaning: aggregation of fibrin, platelets, and erythrocytes in an intact artery or vein

thymocyte.meaning: immature T cell found in the thymus

thymosins.meaning: hormones produced and secreted by the thymus that play an important role in the development and differentiation of T cells

thymus.meaning: primary lymphoid organ; where T lymphocytes proliferate and mature

thyrocervical artery.meaning: arises from the subclavian artery; supplies blood to the thyroid, the cervical region, the upper back, and shoulder

thyrohyoid.meaning: muscle that depresses the hyoid bone and elevates the larynx’s thyroid cartilage

thyroid cartilage.meaning: largest piece of cartilage that makes up the larynx and consists of two lamine

thyroid gland.meaning: large endocrine gland responsible for the synthesis of thyroid hormones

thyroid-stimulating hormone.meaning: anterior pituitary hormone that triggers secretion of thyroid hormones by the thyroid gland (also called thyrotropin)

thyroxine.meaning: (also, tetraiodothyronine, T4) amino acid–derived thyroid hormone that is more abundant but less potent than T3 and often converted to T3 by target cells

tibia.meaning: shin bone; the large, weight-bearing bone located on the medial side of the leg

tibial collateral ligament.meaning: extrinsic ligament of knee joint that spans from the medial epicondyle of the femur to the medial tibia; resists hyperextension and rotation of extended knee

tibial nerve.meaning: systemic nerve of the posterior leg that begins as part of the sciatic nerve

tibial tuberosity.meaning: elevated area on the anterior surface of the proximal tibia

tibialis anterior.meaning: muscle located on the lateral surface of the tibia

tibialis posterior.meaning: muscle that plantar flexes and inverts the foot

tidal volume.meaning: amount of air that normally enters the lungs during quiet breathing

tight junction.meaning: forms an impermeable barrier between cells

tissue.meaning: group of similar or closely related cells that act together to perform a specific function

tissue factor.meaning: protein thromboplastin, which initiates the extrinsic pathway when released in response to tissue damage

tissue membrane.meaning: thin layer or sheet of cells that covers the outside of the body, organs, and internal cavities

tissue typing.meaning: typing of MHC molecules between a recipient and donor for use in a potential transplantation procedure

tongue.meaning: accessory digestive organ of the mouth, the bulk of which is composed of skeletal muscle

tonsils.meaning: lymphoid nodules associated with the nasopharynx

total dead space.meaning: sum of the anatomical dead space and alveolar dead space

total lung capacity.meaning: total amount of air that can be held in the lungs; sum of TV, ERV, IRV, and RV

total pressure.meaning: sum of all the partial pressures of a gaseous mixture

totipotent.meaning: embryonic cells that have the ability to differentiate into any type of cell and organ in the body

totipotent stem cell.meaning: embryonic stem cell that is capable of differentiating into any and all cells of the body; enabling the full development of an organism

trabeculae.meaning: (singular = trabecula) spikes or sections of the lattice-like matrix in spongy bone

trabeculae carneae.meaning: ridges of muscle covered by endocardium located in the ventricles

trachea.meaning: tube composed of cartilaginous rings and supporting tissue that connects the lung bronchi and the larynx; provides a route for air to enter and exit the lung

trachealis muscle.meaning: smooth muscle located in the fibroelastic membrane of the trachea

tract.meaning: bundle of axons in the central nervous system having the same function and point of origin

transamination.meaning: transfer of an amine group from one molecule to another as a way to turn nitrogen waste into ammonia so that it can enter the urea cycle

transcription.meaning: process of producing an mRNA molecule that is complementary to a particular gene of DNA

transcription factor.meaning: one of the proteins that regulate the transcription of genes

transduction.meaning: process of changing an environmental stimulus into the electrochemical signals of the nervous system

transfer rna.meaning: molecules of RNA that serve to bring amino acids to a growing polypeptide strand and properly place them into the sequence

transferrin.meaning: plasma protein that binds reversibly to iron and distributes it throughout the body

transient ischaemic attack.meaning: temporary disruption of blood flow to the brain in which symptoms occur rapidly but last only a short time

transitional epithelium.meaning: form of stratified epithelium found in the urinary tract, characterised by an apical layer of cells that change shape in response to the presence of urine

translation.meaning: process of producing a protein from the nucleotide sequence code of an mRNA transcript

transpulmonary pressure.meaning: pressure difference between the intrapleural and intra-alveolar pressures

transverse colon.meaning: part of the colon between the ascending colon and the descending colon

transverse foramen.meaning: opening found only in the transverse processes of cervical vertebrae

transverse plane.meaning: two-dimensional, horizontal plane that divides the body or organ into superior and inferior portions

transverse process.meaning: paired bony processes that extends laterally from the vertebral arch of a vertebra

transverse sinuses.meaning: pair of enlarged veins near the lambdoid suture that drain the occipital, sagittal, and straight sinuses, and leads to the sigmoid sinuses

transversospinales.meaning: muscles that originate at the transverse processes and insert at the spinous processes of the vertebrae

transversus abdominis.meaning: deep layer of the abdomen that has fascicles arranged transversely around the abdomen

trapezium.meaning: from the lateral side, the first of the four distal carpal bones; articulates with the scaphoid proximally, the first and second metacarpals distally, and the trapezoid medially

trapezius.meaning: muscle that stabilises the upper part of the back

trapezoid.meaning: from the lateral side, the second of the four distal carpal bones; articulates with the scaphoid proximally, the second metacarpal distally, the trapezium laterally, and the capitate medially

triad.meaning: the grouping of one T-tubule and two terminal cisternae

tricarboxylic acid cycle.meaning: also called the Krebs cycle or the citric acid cycle; converts pyruvate into CO2 and high-energy FADH2, NADH, and ATP molecules

triceps brachii.meaning: three-headed muscle that extends the forearm

tricuspid valve.meaning: term used most often in clinical settings for the right atrioventricular valve

trigeminal ganglion.meaning: sensory ganglion that contributes sensory fibres to the trigeminal nerve

trigeminal nerve.meaning: fifth cranial nerve; responsible for cutaneous sensation of the face and contraction of the muscles of mastication

triglyceride.meaning: lipid compound composed of a glycerol molecule bonded with three fatty acid chains

triglycerides.meaning: lipids, or fats, consisting of three fatty acid chains attached to a glycerol backbone

trigone.meaning: area at the base of the bladder marked by the two ureters in the posterior–lateral aspect and the urethral orifice in the anterior aspect oriented like points on a triangle

triiodothyronine.meaning: (also, T3) amino acid–derived thyroid hormone that is less abundant but more potent than T4

trimester.meaning: division of the duration of a pregnancy into three 3-month terms

triplet.meaning: consecutive sequence of three nucleotides on a DNA molecule that, when transcribed into an mRNA codon, corresponds to a particular amino acid

triquetrum.meaning: from the lateral side, the third of the four proximal carpal bones; articulates with the lunate laterally, the hamate distally, and has a facet for the pisiform

trochlea.meaning: pulley-shaped region located medially at the distal end of the humerus; articulates at the elbow with the trochlear notch of the ulna

trochlear nerve.meaning: fourth cranial nerve; responsible for contraction of one of the extraocular muscles

trochlear notch.meaning: large, C-shaped depression located on the anterior side of the proximal ulna; articulates at the elbow with the trochlea of the humerus

trophoblast.meaning: fluid-filled shell of squamous cells destined to become the chorionic villi, placenta, and associated fetal membranes

tropomyosin.meaning: regulatory protein that covers myosin-binding sites to prevent actin from binding to myosin

troponin.meaning: regulatory protein that binds to actin, tropomyosin, and calcium

true labour.meaning: regular contractions that immediately precede childbirth; they do not abate with hydration or rest, and they become more frequent and powerful with time

true ribs.meaning: vertebrosternal ribs 1–7 that attach via their costal cartilage directly to the sternum

true vocal cord.meaning: one of the pair of folded, white membranes that have a free inner edge that oscillates as air passes through to produce sound

truncus arteriosus.meaning: portion of the primitive heart that will eventually divide and give rise to the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk

trunk.meaning: large vessel that gives rise to smaller vessels

trypsin.meaning: pancreatic enzyme that activates chymotrypsin and digests protein

tubercle of the rib.meaning: small bump on the posterior side of a rib for articulation with the transverse process of a thoracic vertebra

tubuloglomerular feedback.meaning: feedback mechanism involving the JGA; macula densa cells monitor Na+ concentration in the terminal portion of the ascending loop of Henle and act to cause vasoconstriction or vasodilation of afferent and efferent arterioles to alter GFR

tunica externa.meaning: (also, tunica adventitia) outermost layer or tunic of a vessel (except capillaries)

tunica intima.meaning: (also, tunica interna) innermost lining or tunic of a vessel

tunica media.meaning: middle layer or tunic of a vessel (except capillaries)

twitch.meaning: single contraction produced by one action potential

type i alveolar cell.meaning: squamous epithelial cells that are the major cell type in the alveolar wall; highly permeable to gases

type i hypersensitivity.meaning: immediate response mediated by mast cell degranulation caused by the crosslinking of the antigen-specific IgE molecules on the mast cell surface

type ii alveolar cell.meaning: cuboidal epithelial cells that are the minor cell type in the alveolar wall; secrete pulmonary surfactant

type ii hypersensitivity.meaning: cell damage caused by the binding of antibody and the activation of complement, usually against red blood cells

type iii hypersensitivity.meaning: damage to tissues caused by the deposition of antibody-antigen (immune) complexes followed by the activation of complement

ulna.meaning: bone located on the medial side of the forearm

ulnar artery.meaning: formed at the bifurcation of the brachial artery; parallels the ulna; gives off smaller branches until it reaches the carpal region where it fuses with the radial artery to form the superficial and deep palmar arches; supplies blood to the lower arm and carpal region

ulnar collateral ligament.meaning: intrinsic ligament on the medial side of the elbow joint; spans from the medial epicondyle of the humerus to the medial ulna

ulnar nerve.meaning: systemic nerve of the arm located close to the ulna, a bone of the forearm

ulnar notch of the radius.meaning: shallow, smooth area located on the medial side of the distal radius; articulates with the head of the ulna at the distal radioulnar joint

ulnar tuberosity.meaning: roughened area located on the anterior, proximal ulna inferior to the coronoid process

ulnar vein.meaning: parallels the ulna and ulnar artery; arises from the palmar venous arches and leads to the brachial vein

ultrasonography.meaning: application of ultrasonic waves to visualise subcutaneous body structures such as tendons and organs

umami.meaning: taste submodality for sensitivity to the concentration of amino acids; also called the savoury sense

umbilical arteries.meaning: pair of vessels that runs within the umbilical cord and carries fetal blood low in oxygen and high in waste to the placenta for exchange with maternal blood

umbilical cord.meaning: connection between the developing conceptus and the placenta; carries deoxygenated blood and wastes from the fetus and returns nutrients and oxygen from the mother

umbilical vein.meaning: single vessel that originates in the placenta and runs within the umbilical cord, carrying oxygen- and nutrient-rich blood to the fetal heart

uniaxial joint.meaning: type of diarthrosis; joint that allows for motion within only one plane (one axis)

unipennate.meaning: pennate muscle that has fascicles located on one side of the tendon

unipolar.meaning: shape of a neuron which has only one process that includes both the axon and dendrite

unipotent.meaning: describes the condition of being committed to a single specialised cell type

upper esophageal sphincter.meaning: skeletal muscle sphincter that regulates food movement from the pharynx to the oesophagus

upper motor neuron.meaning: first neuron in the motor command pathway with its cell body in the cerebral cortex that synapses on the lower motor neuron in the spinal cord

upregulation.meaning: increase in the number of hormone receptors, typically in response to chronically reduced levels of a hormone

urea cycle.meaning: process that converts potentially toxic nitrogen waste into urea that can be eliminated through the kidneys

urethra.meaning: transports urine from the bladder to the outside environment

urinalysis.meaning: analysis of urine to diagnose disease

urochrome.meaning: heme-derived pigment that imparts the typical yellow colour of urine

urogenital triangle.meaning: anterior triangle of the perineum that includes the external genitals

uterine tubes.meaning: (also, fallopian tubes or oviducts) ducts that facilitate transport of an ovulated oocyte to the uterus

uterus.meaning: muscular hollow organ in which a fertilised egg develops into a fetus

utricle.meaning: structure of the inner ear responsible for transducing linear acceleration in the horizontal plane

vagina.meaning: tunnel-like organ that provides access to the uterus for the insertion of semen and from the uterus for the birth of a baby

vagus nerve.meaning: tenth cranial nerve; responsible for the autonomic control of organs in the thoracic and upper abdominal cavities

valence shell.meaning: outermost electron shell of an atom

valsalva’s manoeuvre.meaning: voluntary contraction of the diaphragm and abdominal wall muscles and closing of the glottis, which increases intra-abdominal pressure and facilitates defecation

valve.meaning: in the cardiovascular system, a specialised structure located within the heart or vessels that ensures one-way flow of blood

variable region domain.meaning: part of a lymphocyte antigen receptor that varies considerably between different receptor types

varicosity.meaning: enlargement of neurons that release neurotransmitters into synaptic clefts

vasa recta.meaning: branches of the efferent arterioles that parallel the course of the loops of Henle and are continuous with the peritubular capillaries; with the glomerulus, form a portal system

vasa vasorum.meaning: small blood vessels located within the walls or tunics of larger vessels that supply nourishment to and remove wastes from the cells of the vessels

vascular shock.meaning: type of shock that occurs when arterioles lose their normal muscular tone and dilate dramatically

vascular shunt.meaning: continuation of the metarteriole and thoroughfare channel that allows blood to bypass the capillary beds to flow directly from the arterial to the venous circulation

vascular spasm.meaning: initial step in haemostasis, in which the smooth muscle in the walls of the ruptured or damaged blood vessel contracts

vascular tone.meaning: contractile state of smooth muscle in a blood vessel

vascular tubes.meaning: rudimentary blood vessels in a developing fetus

vascular tunic.meaning: middle layer of the eye primarily composed of connective tissue with a rich blood supply

vasoconstriction.meaning: constriction of the smooth muscle of a blood vessel, resulting in a decreased vascular diameter

vasomotion.meaning: irregular, pulsating flow of blood through capillaries and related structures

vasomotor nerves.meaning: preganglionic sympathetic fibres that cause the constriction of blood vessels in response to signals from the cardiovascular centre

vastus intermedius.meaning: quadricep muscle that is between the vastus lateralis and vastus medialis and is deep to the rectus femoris

vastus lateralis.meaning: quadricep muscle on the lateral aspect of the thigh

vastus medialis.meaning: quadricep muscle on the medial aspect of the thigh

vein.meaning: blood vessel that conducts blood toward the heart

venous reserve.meaning: volume of blood contained within systemic veins in the integument, bone marrow, and liver that can be returned to the heart for circulation, if needed

ventilation.meaning: movement of air into and out of the lungs; consists of inspiration and expiration

ventral.meaning: describes the front or direction toward the front of the body; also referred to as anterior

ventral (anterior) nerve root.meaning: axons emerging from the anterior or lateral horns of the spinal cord

ventral cavity.meaning: larger body cavity located anterior to the posterior (dorsal) body cavity; includes the serous membrane-lined pleural cavities for the lungs, pericardial cavity for the heart, and peritoneal cavity for the abdominal and pelvic organs; also referred to as anterior body cavity

ventral posterior nucleus.meaning: nucleus in the thalamus that is the target of gustatory sensations and projects to the cerebral cortex

ventral respiratory group.meaning: region of the medulla oblongata that stimulates the contraction of the accessory muscles involved in respiration to induce forced inspiration and expiration

ventral stream.meaning: connections between cortical areas from the occipital lobe to the temporal lobe that are responsible for identification of visual stimuli

ventricle.meaning: central cavity within the brain where CSF is produced and circulates

ventricles.meaning: remnants of the hollow centre of the neural tube that are spaces for cerebrospinal fluid to circulate through the brain

ventricular ejection phase.meaning: second phase of ventricular systole during which blood is pumped from the ventricle

venule.meaning: small vessel leading from the capillaries to veins

vermis.meaning: prominent ridge along the midline of the cerebellum that is referred to as the spinocerebellum

vernix caseosa.meaning: waxy, cheese-like substance that protects the delicate fetal skin until birth

vertebra.meaning: individual bone in the neck and back regions of the vertebral column

vertebral (spinal) canal.meaning: bony passageway within the vertebral column for the spinal cord that is formed by the series of individual vertebral foramina

vertebral arch.meaning: bony arch formed by the posterior portion of each vertebra that surrounds and protects the spinal cord

vertebral arteries.meaning: arteries that ascend along either side of the vertebral column through the transverse foramina of the cervical vertebrae and enter the cranium through the foramen magnum

vertebral artery.meaning: arises from the subclavian artery and passes through the vertebral foramen through the foramen magnum to the brain; joins with the internal carotid artery to form the arterial circle; supplies blood to the brain and spinal cord

vertebral column.meaning: entire sequence of bones that extend from the skull to the tailbone

vertebral foramen.meaning: opening associated with each vertebra defined by the vertebral arch that provides passage for the spinal cord

vertebral vein.meaning: arises from the base of the brain and the cervical region of the spinal cord; passes through the intervertebral foramina in the cervical vertebrae; drains smaller veins from the cranium, spinal cord, and vertebrae, and leads to the brachiocephalic vein; counterpart of the vertebral artery

vesicle.meaning: membrane-bound structure that contains materials within or outside of the cell

vestibular fold.meaning: part of the folded region of the glottis composed of mucous membrane; supports the epiglottis during swallowing

vestibular ganglion.meaning: location of neuronal cell bodies that transmit equilibrium information along the eighth cranial nerve

vestibular nuclei.meaning: targets of the vestibular component of the eighth cranial nerve

vestibule.meaning: in the ear, the portion of the inner ear responsible for the sense of equilibrium

vestibulo-ocular reflex.meaning: reflex based on connections between the vestibular system and the cranial nerves of eye movements that ensures images are stabilised on the retina as the head and body move

vestibulocerebellum.meaning: flocculonodular lobe of the cerebellum named for the vestibular input from the eighth cranial nerve

vestibulocochlear nerve.meaning: eighth cranial nerve; responsible for the sensations of hearing and balance

vestibulospinal tract.meaning: extrapyramidal connections between the vestibular nuclei in the brainstem and spinal cord that modulate movement and contribute to balance on the basis of the sense of equilibrium

villus.meaning: projection of the mucosa of the small intestine

visceral branches.meaning: branches of the descending aorta that supply blood to the viscera

visceral muscle.meaning: smooth muscle found in the walls of visceral organs

visceral pleura.meaning: innermost layer of the pleura that is superficial to the lungs and extends into the lung fissures

visceral reflex.meaning: reflex involving an internal organ as the effector, under the control of the autonomic nervous system

visceral sense.meaning: sense associated with the internal organs

vision.meaning: special sense of sight based on transduction of light stimuli

visual acuity.meaning: property of vision related to the sharpness of focus, which varies in relation to retinal position

vital capacity.meaning: sum of TV, ERV, and IRV, which is all the volumes that participate in gas exchange

vitamin d.meaning: compound that aids absorption of calcium and phosphates in the intestine to improve bone health

vitamins.meaning: organic compounds required by the body to perform biochemical reactions like metabolism and bone, cell, and tissue growth

vitiligo.meaning: skin condition in which melanocytes in certain areas lose the ability to produce melanin, possibly due an autoimmune reaction that leads to loss of colour in patches

vitreous humour.meaning: viscous fluid that fills the posterior chamber of the eye

voltage-gated channel.meaning: ion channel that opens because of a change in the charge distributed across the membrane where it is located

voltage-gated sodium channels.meaning: membrane proteins that open sodium channels in response to a sufficient voltage change, and initiate and transmit the action potential as Na+ enters through the channel

voluntary phase.meaning: initial phase of deglutition, in which the bolus moves from the mouth to the oropharynx

vomer bone.meaning: unpaired bone that forms the inferior and posterior portions of the nasal septum

wave summation.meaning: addition of successive neural stimuli to produce greater contraction

weber test.meaning: use of a tuning fork to test the laterality of hearing loss by placing it at several locations on the midline of the skull

wernicke’s area.meaning: region at the posterior end of the lateral sulcus in which speech comprehension is localised

white blood cells.meaning: (also, leukocytes) one of the formed elements of blood that provides defence against disease agents and foreign materials

white matter.meaning: regions of the nervous system containing mostly myelinated axons, making the tissue appear white because of the high lipid content of myelin

white rami communicantes.meaning: (singular = ramus communicans) myelinated structures that provide a short connection from a sympathetic chain ganglion to the spinal nerve that contains the preganglionic sympathetic fibre

wolffian duct.meaning: duct system present in the embryo that will eventually form the internal male reproductive structures

working memory.meaning: function of the prefrontal cortex to maintain a representation of information that is not in the immediate environment

wound contraction.meaning: process whereby the borders of a wound are physically drawn together

x-linked.meaning: pattern of inheritance in which an allele is carried on the X chromosome of the 23rd pair

x-linked dominant.meaning: pattern of dominant inheritance that corresponds to a gene on the X chromosome of the 23rd pair

x-linked recessive.meaning: pattern of recessive inheritance that corresponds to a gene on the X chromosome of the 23rd pair

x-ray.meaning: form of high energy electromagnetic radiation with a short wavelength capable of penetrating solids and ionising gases; used in medicine as a diagnostic aid to visualise body structures such as bones

xiphoid process.meaning: small process that forms the inferior tip of the sternum

yellow marrow.meaning: connective tissue in the interior cavity of a bone where fat is stored

yolk sac.meaning: membrane associated with primitive circulation to the developing embryo; source of the first blood cells and germ cells and contributes to the umbilical cord structure

zona fasciculata.meaning: intermediate region of the adrenal cortex that produce hormones called glucocorticoids

zona glomerulosa.meaning: most superficial region of the adrenal cortex, which produces the hormones collectively referred to as mineralocorticoids

zona pellucida.meaning: thick, gel-like glycoprotein membrane that coats the oocyte and must be penetrated by sperm before fertilisation can occur

zona reticularis.meaning: deepest region of the adrenal cortex, which produces the steroid sex hormones called androgens

zone of calcified matrix.meaning: region of the epiphyseal plate closest to the diaphyseal end; functions to connect the epiphyseal plate to the diaphysis

zone of maturation and hypertrophy.meaning: region of the epiphyseal plate where chondrocytes from the proliferative zone grow and mature and contribute to the longitudinal growth of the epiphyseal plate

zonule fibres.meaning: fibrous connections between the ciliary body and the lens

zygapophysial joints.meaning: facet joints; plane joints between the superior and inferior articular processes of adjacent vertebrae that provide for only limited motions between the vertebrae

zygomatic arch.meaning: elongated, free-standing arch on the lateral skull, formed anteriorly by the temporal process of the zygomatic bone and posteriorly by the zygomatic process of the temporal bone

zygomatic bone.meaning: cheekbone; paired bones that contribute to the lateral orbit and anterior zygomatic arch

zygomatic process of the temporal bone.term: zygomatic process of the temporal bone
zygomatic process of the temporal bone.meaning: extension from the temporal bone that forms the posterior portion of the zygomatic arch

zygote.meaning: fertilised egg; a diploid cell resulting from the fertilisation of haploid gametes from the male and female lines

α-dextrinase.meaning: brush border enzyme that acts on α-dextrins
